headline: NA body wants railways land retrieved from private, govt departments
description: ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly Standing Committee on Railways was informed on Tuesday that out of 19,594 acres of...
author: Aamir Yasin
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly Standing Committee on Railways was informed on Tuesday that out of 19,594 acres of railways land, approximately 951.28 acres were under illegal occupation of the private sector while 307 acres were encroached upon by the government.

However, as many as 363.907 acres of land had been retrieved during the last four years.

Furthermore, during July to October 2026, encroachments covering approximately 8.992 acres were removed, with an estimated value of Rs305.67 million.

The Ministry also shared a comprehensive schedule for the removal of further encroachments during November 2026.

The meeting was held at the Parliament House with MNA Ramesh Lal, in the chair.

The National Assembly Standing Committee on Railways emphasized the importance of protecting valuable railway land from encroachments, ensuring effective coordination with provincial and local administrations, expediting land retrieval operations and taking concrete measures to improve the land safety.

It also stressed the need for timely implementation of the Committee’s previous recommendations and further strengthening the overall operational efficiency of Pakistan Railways.

The committee reviewed matters relating to Pakistan Railways, including the Railway Board Bill, 2026, encroachments on railway land in Karachi Division, and recent railway accidents across the country.

The meeting considered the Bill titled ‘The Railway Board Bill, 2026’ (Government Bill) and decided to defer its consideration until the next meeting of the committee. The meeting was apprised on recent railway accidents across the country.

It was informed that 89 accidents had been reported from January 1 to November 2, compared to 92 accidents during the corresponding period of 2025. The major causes included track-related issues, rolling stock defects, human errors, road users’ violations, sabotage, natural calamities and other operational failures.

The Ministry officials highlighted that ageing railway infrastructure, inadequate development funding, trespassing, violations at level crossings and foggy weather were among the contributing factors to accidents.

Pakistan Railways is striving to reduce the accident ratio to below 0.19pc under its strategic roadmap.

The meeting was attended by MNAs Ibrar Ahmed, Waseem Qadir, Munir Iqbal, Syeda Amnah Batool, Zulfikar Bachani, Sadiq Ali Memon, Dr. Mahreen Razzaq Bhutto, Syed Waseem Hussain and Ahmed Saleem Siddiqui. Officers of the Ministry of Railways and Pakistan Railways also attended the meeting.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Murree admin conducts snow emergency drills
description: Multi-agency exercises to enable proactive response during winter, ensure tourist safety
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
RAWALPINDI: Mock exercises were conducted in Murree with the objective of evaluating the preparedness and overall operational readiness of all relevant departments to effectively handle emergencies arising during snowfall and adverse weather conditions.

Under the direction of Murree Deputy Commissioner Agha Zaheer Abbas Shirazi, the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) organised mock emergency exercises in preparation for the 2026-27 winter and snowfall season.

The drills included practical demonstrations of various response operations, such as: reaching citizens and tourists stranded in the snow; relocating affected individuals to safe areas; providing emergency shelter; responding promptly to traffic accidents; delivering medical aid to those affected; clearing roads blocked by congestion; removing snow from highways; clearing fallen trees, electricity poles and utility lines from roads; and restoring traffic flow in the event of landslides.

PDMA Punjab, Rescue 1122, Police Department, Civil Defence, Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (Pera) force, the Punjab Tourism Squad, the Highway Department, the Health Department, the Forest Department, the Meteorological Department, the Municipal Corporation, Wapda, and other relevant allied departments participated actively in the mock exercises, utilising their available resources. Heads of all the participating departments were also present on the occasion.

Multi-agency exercises to enable proactive response during winter, ensure tourist safety

District Emergency Officer for Rescue 1122, Engineer Kamran Rashid, briefed Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) Kamran Sagheer on the various stages of the mock exercises and provided a briefing on the response mechanism.

Speaking on the occasion, the additional deputy commissioner stated that the district administration’s top priority is to ensure the provision of all possible facilities and prompt assistance to both tourists visiting Murree and local residents during the snowfall season.

To this end, personnel from the allied departments will diligently perform their duties at all facilitation centres, and instructions have been issued for all relevant departments to remain on high alert.

He further added that such emergency mock exercises strengthen coordination and synergy among various agencies, enabling proactive preparedness for unforeseen situations such as heavy snowfall or severe weather.

He expressed satisfaction with the ‘Snowfall Season Emergency Response Plan’ prepared by the District Disaster Management Authority.

He directed all relevant departments to maintain mutual communication and effective coordination, ensuring that, through a well-devised strategy during the winter and snowfall season, the safety, convenience, and timely assistance of citizens and tourists are guaranteed.

headline: Exhibition explores Iqbal’s ‘Saqi Nama’ through paintings
description: ISLAMABAD: An exhibition titled ‘Saqi Nama’ opened on Tuesday at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA)....
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: An exhibition titled ‘Saqi Nama’ opened on Tuesday at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA).

The exhibition commemorated the 150th birth anniversary of Allama Mohammad Iqbal.

Celebrating the poetic vision and philosophical legacy of Allama Iqbal, the exhibition brought together the artistic expressions of three artists, Geytee Ara, Lubna Jehangir and Zarar Haider Babry, in response to Allama Mohammad Iqbal’s poem. It will remain open until November 18.

‘Saqi Nama’ brings together three artists, each with a distinct voice, perspective, and medium, in response to a single poem.

Iqbal’s ‘Saqi Nama’ is among the most celebrated poems in Urdu and Persian literary tradition.

The artists approached the poem with reverence and with an awareness of the master artists who had interpreted it before them. Each work takes a single couplet as its point of departure and becomes an independent encounter with the verse.

Geytee Ara explores the ways material carries memory. Through form, surface and touch, she seeks a language in which inherited ideas can meet the urgency of the present, and finds in ‘Saqi Nama’ a space for reflection on selfhood, renewal and the courage to become.

Lubna Jehangir returns to rhythm, movement, and illumination. Colour becomes both atmosphere and inquiry, a way to approach the poem’s inner landscapes while allowing each work to keep its own silence and mystery.

Zarar Haider Babry considers ascent, struggle and transformation as visual states. Iqbal’s poetry is his point of departure, while line, colour, and gesture create an independent encounter with energy, aspiration, and the evolving self.

Together, these works suggest that the courage to become belongs to every stage of life. They invite the viewer to pause, look closely, and take the poem’s cup as an invitation to see oneself anew.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

article_html:
ISLAMABAD: An exhibition titled ‘Saqi Nama’ opened on Tuesday at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA).

The exhibition commemorated the 150th birth anniversary of Allama Mohammad Iqbal.

Celebrating the poetic vision and philosophical legacy of Allama Iqbal, the exhibition brought together the artistic expressions of three artists, Geytee Ara, Lubna Jehangir and Zarar Haider Babry, in response to Allama Mohammad Iqbal’s poem. It will remain open until November 18.

‘Saqi Nama’ brings together three artists, each with a distinct voice, perspective, and medium, in response to a single poem.

Iqbal’s ‘Saqi Nama’ is among the most celebrated poems in Urdu and Persian literary tradition.

The artists approached the poem with reverence and with an awareness of the master artists who had interpreted it before them. Each work takes a single couplet as its point of departure and becomes an independent encounter with the verse.

Geytee Ara explores the ways material carries memory. Through form, surface and touch, she seeks a language in which inherited ideas can meet the urgency of the present, and finds in ‘Saqi Nama’ a space for reflection on selfhood, renewal and the courage to become.

Lubna Jehangir returns to rhythm, movement, and illumination. Colour becomes both atmosphere and inquiry, a way to approach the poem’s inner landscapes while allowing each work to keep its own silence and mystery.

Zarar Haider Babry considers ascent, struggle and transformation as visual states. Iqbal’s poetry is his point of departure, while line, colour, and gesture create an independent encounter with energy, aspiration, and the evolving self.

Together, these works suggest that the courage to become belongs to every stage of life. They invite the viewer to pause, look closely, and take the poem’s cup as an invitation to see oneself anew.

headline: Government committed to improving road network: minister
description: TAXILA: Minister of State for Law and Justice Barrister Aqeel Malik here said that the government was committed to...
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
TAXILA: Minister of State for Law and Justice Barrister Aqeel Malik here said that the government was committed to expanding development opportunities and improving basic facilities, particularly road networks, to facilitate commuters and stimulate local economic activity.

He was addressing a gathering after performing the groundbreaking of the rehabilitation of Mohra Chowk-Gadwal crossing road near Wah on Tuesday.

The project of 3.50 kilometre-long road aims to improve local connectivity, upgrade road infrastructure

and provide residents with safer, smoother and more convenient travelling facilities which would be completed at a cost of Rs304.597 million in three months.

Mr Malik added that the improvement of basic infrastructure, construction of quality roads and provision of modern transport facilities were among his foremost priorities. He maintained that resolving public grievances, accelerating development across the constituency and ensuring access to essential amenities remained central to his political agenda.

He said he believed in translating commitments made to the electorate into practical initiatives rather than mere political promises.

Development projects would continue in all areas without discrimination to ensure that people

received improved civic facilities, he added.

The minister emphasised that public representatives had a responsibility to respond to the needs of their constituents through tangible development measures, adding that the government remained committed to improving infrastructure and addressing longstanding public concerns.

Speaking on this occasion, chairman standing committee on finance Mohsin Ayub Khan underscored the importance of infrastructure development, saying that quality roads were fundamental to easing transportation difficulties and improving the daily lives of local communities.

He described the Mohra Chowk-Gadwal railway crossing road project as an important initiative towards strengthening the area’s road network and facilitating commuters.

He said development schemes should be undertaken in accordance with local requirements so that their benefits could reach people at the grassroots level.

He expressed optimism that the project would improve connectivity between the localities served by the route, reduce commuting difficulties and provide a more convenient travelling experience to residents.

headline: President extends felicitations on Poland’s Independence Day
description: ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zardari has felicitated Poland on its National Independence Day, conveying his highest...
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zardari has felicitated Poland on its National Independence Day, conveying his highest regards to his counterpart Karol Nawrocki and expressing optimism for future bilateral relations. In a letter addressed to President Nawrocki, President Zardari conveyed greetings on behalf of the government and people of Pakistan, and in his personal capacity.

He noted that Pakistan and Poland enjoy longstanding and cordial relations, founded on mutual respect, goodwill and a shared commitment to peace and international cooperation.

He expressed confidence that bilateral relations would continue to strengthen through enhanced engagement and expanded cooperation in areas of mutual interest for the mutual benefit of the two peoples.

headline: CDA plans electric bus service exclusively for women
description: Civic agency in process of acquiring 30 electric pink buses, says official
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) is planning to launch an exclusive electric bus service for women.

If all goes as planned, the civic agency will introduce the service with 30 new pink buses.

Sources said that on the direction of the federal government and the Interior Ministry, the CDA was in the process of engaging its partners for acquiring 30 electric pink buses for the new service.

They said that the CDA will engage Heavy Industries Taxila (HIT) for importing the buses, likely from China, on the same pattern of the existing 160 buses of the Electric Bus Service.

The CDA through its contractor has already been running an electric bus service on over 20 routes in Islamabad with a fleet of over 160 buses with overwhelming response from citizens.

Civic agency in process of acquiring 30 electric pink buses, says official

However, sources said that it had been noticed that women and girls faced difficulty for getting space in these 60 buses during peak hours.

Therefore, it has been decided that an exclusive bus service with 30 pink buses will be introduced for women only.

“Yes, we have decided to introduce pink bus service as well. We have directed the concerned wing of the CDA to bring a summary for board and after approval of board, we will move forward to engage HIT for importing buses from China,” said a senior officer of CDA.

He said that the response of citizens to the existing bus service was overwhelming and highly encouraging, therefore, “we are going to introduce a dedicated bus service for women, which will ply on different routes,” he said.

To a query, the officer said the buses will be ply on same routes where existing bus service is in operation, but in case of a neednew routes could also be added.

It is relevant to note that a few months ago the CDA had decided to start a double-decker bus service for promotion of tourism in Islamabad.

The CDA had approached HIT for a feasibility study and estimate for procuring the buses.

Initially, the CDA plans to start the service of double-decker with four buses for the city tour – a 25km trip – starting from F-9 Park and covering all important points, including Faisal Mosque, Lok Virsa and Shakarparian.

After this announcement of double-decker, the CDA recently got approval from its board and subsequently the Development Working Party (DWP) also approved the PC-I of double-decker bus service.

“I guess, the double-decker bus service will be started soon as we are at an advanced stage. But pink bus service will also be introduced as soon as possible, may be within three months,” the officer said.

headline: Two killed in separate incidents
description: RAWALPINDI: A woman was killed in a road accident in Chontra area, while a man drowned in Rama Dam near Islamabad...
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
RAWALPINDI: A woman was killed in a road accident in Chontra area, while a man drowned in Rama Dam near Islamabad International Airport on Tuesday.

Police said a woman identified as Farah Bibi, 35, a resident of Dhallowali Mohra, Chontra, sustained fatal injuries after being hit by a tractor. Later, the police shifted her body to the District Headquarters Hospital for postmortem.

In another incident, police said Musa Nazakat, 25, a resident of Dora Islamabad, drowned in Rama Dam while he was fishing.

Later, Rescue 1122 divers from Fatehjang reached the spot and conducted a search operation.

During the operation, the deceased’s body was recovered from the water and was handed over to the deceased’s heirs after completion of legal formalities.

headline: Minister asked to enforce protection of breast-feeding ordinance
description: ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on National Health Services has called on Federal Health Minister Mustafa...
author: Ikram Junaidi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on National Health Services has called on Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal to enforce the Protection of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance, 2002, warning that weak implementation undermines child health.

In a letter to Health Minister Mustafa Kamal and available with Dawn, the committee chairman Senator Amir Waliuddin Chishti expressed concern over the law’s lack of enforcement despite being in place for over 20 years. The committee, which met on Nov 3 reviewed the regulation of infant formula marketing as substitute for breast milk.

The letter highlighted the need for the National Infant Feeding Board to be operational asking for details on its formation, meetings and activities. The committee also demanded information on measures taken to stop prohibited advertising, free samples and misleading claim.

It questioned whether the Supreme Court and Islamabad High Court orders regarding Urdu labelling and warnings on formula milk had been complied with and asked the ministry to report on progress on enforcing court orders.

While acknowledging that infant formula may be necessary in some cases the committee stressed it must only be used under legal and medical guidelines.

The committee has also demanded data on inspections, prosecutions, penalties and the role of enforcement authorities over the three years. It also asked for information on product registration, quality testing and Drap’s role in monitoring.

The ministry was asked to explain coordination with Drap and Pemra to stop banned ads on TV, digital platforms and other media. Senator Chishti urged action—reviving the National Infant Feeding Board appointing enforcement officials and pursuing legal action against violators.

The committee has asked for a response within 15 days including court orders, regulatory directions and a full implementation plan. It also wants a focal officer assigned for coordination and regular reporting.

The chairman emphasised that protecting infants was a duty and that existing laws must be enforced effectively. While talking to Dawn Senator Chishti said that he was very keen to save the babies which is the future of Pakistan.

headline: Projects worth billions launched, no embezzlement of public money: Punjab CM
description: JHELUM: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday announced that the Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence in Jhelum...
author: Hamid Asghar
article_text:
JHELUM: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday announced that the Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence in Jhelum will become operational on December 15.

She also announced the launch of Green Buses in Dina, Sohawa and Pind Dadan Khan in January. She made the announcements while addressing a ceremony held to distribute Honhaar Scholarships and laptops among students in Jhelum.

The chief minister said billions of rupees worth of development projects were being executed, adding that she had not embezzled even a single penny of public money.

“I swear I will not spare any minister if evidence of corruption emerges against them. Those who have objections should explain why they are sitting as ministers. Why don’t they resign and go home?” she asked.

She said those who had earned notoriety for corruption and bribery were still sitting outside the country. “I am not claiming that corruption has been completely eliminated. But when I come to know about corruption in Punjab, I pursue the matter relentlessly. Is there no corruption in other provinces? The people who looted public money and indulged in corruption during 13 to 14 years of rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa are now being exposed.”

She said she was speaking about Punjab, while other provinces were answerable to their own people. Every penny in Punjab was being spent on public welfare and development, she added.

“We will recover the looted money from those who have betrayed public trust.” The chief minister said her government believed in performance rather than rhetoric. The PML-N repeatedly returned to power because of its public service, she added.

“Popularity is reflected in public support. People vote for service, not political narratives.”

Referring to the Lillah-Jhelum Road project, she said some people would now claim ownership of the initiative. “If it was your project, why did you not complete it during your four-year government? They are good at talking but fail to deliver.”

She said her government faced criticism whenever it undertook development work, but remained committed to fulfilling the aspirations of young people. “Let children dream; Maryam Nawaz will work day and night to turn their dreams into reality.”

Addressing female students, she urged them to move forward confidently and not allow anyone to tell them that certain professions or achievements were beyond their reach.

She said more than 100,000 scooters were being provided to students across Punjab, adding that recipients would also receive proper training. Students were being provided free travel facilities on Green Buses across the province.

The chief minister said 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence were being established throughout Punjab. Referring to the school in Attock, she said a private grammar school and a government-run Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence were located side by side, but the government school offered much better facilities. She challenged critics to identify a public-sector school outside Punjab that matched the standard of the Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence.

The schools featured air-conditioned classrooms, modern laboratories and highly qualified faculty, facilities that were not even available at some private schools charging Rs100,000 in fees. She said 50,000 schools across Punjab were providing education to millions of children. “Education is the best investment because every child is an ambassador of Pakistan.”

The chief minister said her government had broken the longstanding tradition of restricting development projects to major cities. She had spent entire days in Sahiwal, Attock and Mandi Bahauddin and would do the same in Jhelum. Young people were previously misled through narratives, but today they could see development taking place for themselves, she added. “The Green Buses operating in Lahore and Rawalpindi are the same as those running in Khushab, Layyah and Bhakkar. There is no discrimination.”

She said thousands of kilometres of roads had been constructed, with more development work carried out in smaller cities than in Lahore. She said patients were receiving free stents, pacemakers and other cardiac treatment at the Jhelum Cath Lab. “Could anyone have imagined receiving such treatment in Jhelum in the past?”

headline: Two killed in separate incidents
description: RAWALPINDI: A woman was killed in a road accident in Chontra area, while a man drowned in Rama Dam near Islamabad...
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
RAWALPINDI: A woman was killed in a road accident in Chontra area, while a man drowned in Rama Dam near Islamabad International Airport on Tuesday.

Police said a woman identified as Farah Bibi, 35, a resident of Dhallowali Mohra, Chontra, sustained fatal injuries after being hit by a tractor. Later, the police shifted her body to the District Headquarters Hospital for postmortem.

In another incident, police said Musa Nazakat, 25, a resident of Dora Islamabad, drowned in Rama Dam while he was fishing.

Later, Rescue 1122 divers from Fatehjang reached the spot and conducted a search operation.

During the operation, the deceased’s body was recovered from the water and was handed over to the deceased’s heirs after completion of legal formalities.

headline: Remand of slain anchorperson’s husband extended for four days
description: RAWALPINDI: The physical remand of the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, who was shot dead at the couple’s home...
author: Mohammad Asghar, Malik Asad
article_text:
RAWALPINDI: The physical remand of the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, who was shot dead at the couple’s home in the Gulshanabad area of Rawalpindi earlier in the week, was extended by four days by a court on Tuesday.

The suspect, Mohammad Ahsan, was produced before Senior Civil Judge Mohammad Nasrullah Wattoo after completion of his one-day physical remand.

During the hearing, the investigating officer informed the court about the progress made in the investigation. He urged the court to extend the remand by seven days in order to interrogate the suspect and complete the investigation.

After examining the record and hearing the suspect, the court observed that he had been nominated in the first information report (FIR) and that a pistol had also been recovered from him.

The court subsequently extended the remand by four days to facilitate the investigation and directed the investigating officer to produce the suspect on Nov 14. The court also directed the police to complete the investigation and submit the relevant record.

No lawyer appeared on behalf of the suspect during the proceedings.

Meanwhile, it emerged that police had decided to conduct a polygraph test of the suspect, amid alleged inconsistencies in his statements during the investigation.

According to the application seeking his physical remand, the polygraph test was scheduled to be conducted at the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) in Lahore on Wednesday (Nov 11).

Investigators expected to receive its report on Saturday, which they said may help them establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

Rabia, who was associated with 92 News and had previously co-hosted a current affairs programme with senior journalists Amir Mateen and Rauf Klasra, was shot dead at her residence on Nov 8.

According to the FIR registered at Saddar Beruni police station on the complaint of her brother Khurram Ahmed, the victim’s mother and sister were present at the house when they heard a gunshot from the bedroom.

The complainant stated that his sister rushed towards the bedroom after hearing the gunshot and found Rabia lying on the floor in a pool of blood. Her husband was allegedly standing nearby, holding a pistol.

Meanwhile, amid reports that the complainant had decided to withdraw the murder case, a senior officer told Dawn that it was now up to the trial court to decide whether to accept the request to withdrawal the case, if such a request was filed.

Police to question Rabia’s brother

Police have decided to interview the brother of the deceased and other family members living with her to ascertain the actual circumstances in which she was killed.

A senior police official told Dawn that there was no scene of anger at crime scene. The pistol was lying loaded when it was aimed on Rabia by her husband who claimed that it went off accidentally, he added.

However, the police will investigate all aspects and will leave nothing behind in the investigation.

The police are expected to visit the house of Rabia on Wednesday to interview the family, including the complaint in the murder case.

Rabia’s mother and sister had been residing with her to look after her two daughters as she also looked after a beauty salon in Islamabad.

Police said none of the family members of Rabia had expressed suspicion on her husband as they believed that it was an accident not a deliberate murder.

However, Senior Superintendent of Police Investigation Saifulla told Dawn that police will investigate the case from all angles and will also question Rabia’s brother.

The suspect, Mohammad Ahsan, was produced before Senior Civil Judge Mohammad Nasrullah Wattoo after completion of his one-day physical remand.

During the hearing, the investigating officer informed the court about the progress made in the investigation. He urged the court to extend the remand by seven days in order to interrogate the suspect and complete the investigation.

After examining the record and hearing the suspect, the court observed that he had been nominated in the first information report (FIR) and that a pistol had also been recovered from him.

The court subsequently extended the remand by four days to facilitate the investigation and directed the investigating officer to produce the suspect on Nov 14. The court also directed the police to complete the investigation and submit the relevant record.

No lawyer appeared on behalf of the suspect during the proceedings.

Meanwhile, it emerged that police had decided to conduct a polygraph test of the suspect, amid alleged inconsistencies in his statements during the investigation.

According to the application seeking his physical remand, the polygraph test was scheduled to be conducted at the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) in Lahore on Wednesday (Nov 11).

Investigators expected to receive its report on Saturday, which they said may help them establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

Rabia, who was associated with 92 News and had previously co-hosted a current affairs programme with senior journalists Amir Mateen and Rauf Klasra, was shot dead at her residence on Nov 8.

According to the FIR registered at Saddar Beruni police station on the complaint of her brother Khurram Ahmed, the victim’s mother and sister were present at the house when they heard a gunshot from the bedroom.

The complainant stated that his sister rushed towards the bedroom after hearing the gunshot and found Rabia lying on the floor in a pool of blood. Her husband was allegedly standing nearby, holding a pistol.

Meanwhile, amid reports that the complainant had decided to withdraw the murder case, a senior officer told Dawn that it was now up to the trial court to decide whether to accept the request to withdrawal the case, if such a request was filed.

Police to question Rabia’s brother

Police have decided to interview the brother of the deceased and other family members living with her to ascertain the actual circumstances in which she was killed.

A senior police official told Dawn that there was no scene of anger at crime scene. The pistol was lying loaded when it was aimed on Rabia by her husband who claimed that it went off accidentally, he added.

However, the police will investigate all aspects and will leave nothing behind in the investigation.

The police are expected to visit the house of Rabia on Wednesday to interview the family, including the complaint in the murder case.

Rabia’s mother and sister had been residing with her to look after her two daughters as she also looked after a beauty salon in Islamabad.

Police said none of the family members of Rabia had expressed suspicion on her husband as they believed that it was an accident not a deliberate murder.

However, Senior Superintendent of Police Investigation Saifulla told Dawn that police will investigate the case from all angles and will also question Rabia’s brother.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: One killed, 47 injured after bus overturns in Murree area
description: According to Murree police, the accident took place when a bus enroute to Miyari overturned after hitting a roadside pillar.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
RAWALPINDI: One person was killed and 47 others were injured when a bus from Gujranwala overturned due to brake failure near Shawala area of Murree on Tuesday.

The bus driver lost his life in the accident while other people, including nine schoolchildren, were injured when they were heading back to Gujranwala from a trip to Murree.

According to Murree police, the accident took place when a bus en route to Miyari overturned after hitting a roadside pillar.

As a result, bus driver Tanveer Hussain, 60,was killed and 47 others, including schoolchildren, parents and teachers, were injured. Four of the injured were in critical condition.

As soon as the accident was reported, Rescue 1122, district and traffic police officials reached the site and started rescue operation to shift the injured trapped in the bus to the hospital.

The injured were shifted to Tehsil Headquarters Hospital by rescue teams and private vehicles. Traffic police appealed to citizens and tourists to avoid unnecessary crowds near the accident site, give way to rescue vehicles and follow traffic police instructions.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Capital police set up dedicated centre for vulnerable minority groups
description: ISLAMABAD:The police in the capital established a dedicated Meesaq Centre at F-6 Police Khidmat Markaz, a...
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD:The police in the capital established a dedicated Meesaq Centre at F-6 Police Khidmat Markaz, a specialised facility designed to protect the rights of religious minorities and streamline their access to essential legal and public services.

The establishment of the Meesaq Centre was announced last month by the Inspector General of Police Islamabad, Mohammad Sohail Chaudhry.

According to the police officials, the centre was made operational at F-6, with more being established at police stations and other police installations.

The minority communities can share their issues and concerns with the police, and law enforcers will address them on a priority basis and ensure better facilities for them.

It is a minority rights and interfaith harmony unit of the Islamabad police. It is being established at the district level and in subdivisions with large populations of minorities, including Christians, and a troubled history of Muslim-Christian relations.

The unit will be manned by officers of Islamabad police belonging to minorities, especially Christians, and will be supervised by senior officers.

All policing services for minorities will be available at the Meesaq Centre. It will also arrange interfaith harmony dialogues, awareness sessions, and meetings.

The centre will also arrange training for teachers and community leaders.

It will also address general grievances of the community and the implementation of the national narrative.

The centre will also raise awareness about religious festivals and offer services for the protection and well-being of minorities. It will also resolve religious and social issues.

The centre will also ensure the safeguarding of religious, social, and civic rights of all minority communities in Islamabad.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Israel parliament divided over role of Arab parties in new govt
description: • Eisenkot targets Netanyahu’s legacy in first session • Ben Gvir heckles Arab leader Yousef Jabareen during swearing-in ceremony
author: AFP
article_text:
• Eisenkot targets Netanyahu’s legacy in first session • Ben Gvir heckles Arab leader Yousef Jabareen during swearing-in ceremony

JERUSALEM: Tensions ran high at the first session of Israel’s parliament on Tuesday as old and new party leaders traded barbs over the possibility of forming a government with the support of Arab lists.

Two Arab parties, the Joint List and Raam, won an unprecedented 19 seats out of the parliament’s 120 in the Oct 27 election, putting them in a position of kingmakers. But in both camps, some view a government that relies on their support with deep suspicion.

During the swearing-in of the new parliament on Tuesday, far-right Israeli leader Itamar Ben Gvir heckled a prominent leader of the Arab-Israeli community.

“Who is he pledging allegiance to, Hamas?” Ben Gvir shouted at Yousef Jabareen, leader of the largest Arab-majority Joint List.

“Anyone who is not loyal shall not be in the Israeli Knesset!” (parliament) he wrote on X shortly after.

A number of lawmakers from the Joint List left the hall during the Israeli anthem, apparently to avoid standing up for it. The act of protest caused a stir in the chamber.

Netanyahu himself, in a speech during the ceremony, lamented that the two main Arab parties refuse to recognise Israel as a Jewish state — even though Raam leader Mansour Abbas has done so in the past — and claimed they sought to establish an “Islamic state” or a “nationalist Palestinian state… on the ruins of the Jewish state”.

The inauguration comes at a time of political uncertainty, with neither of the two main blocs having secured a majority. President Isaac Herzog tasked ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government on Sunday, following consultations with party leaders last week during which a majority recommended him.

Legislative onslaught

On Tuesday, Eisenkot and his allies launched a legislative onslaught against caretaker Prime Minister Netanyahu’s legacy.

Though questions still linger as to who can form a government, Eisenkot’s broad left-to-right bloc wasted no time in setting the agenda of the new Knesset with a green light from Israeli-Arab lawmakers, whose role has stirred up heated opposition from Netanyahu’s base and even right-wing supporters of Eisenkot.

Eisenkot’s Yashar party said it submitted a slew of proposals before the new parliament, including establishing an independent commission to investigate security failures that allowed the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.

Netanyahu has long opposed such a probe, denying any wrongdoing and calling instead for a politically appointed commission.

Eisenkot’s party also moved for a sweeping repeal of a judicial overhaul implemented by Netanyahu’s government, which had triggered some of Israel’s largest-ever protests before being overshadowed by three years of war.

Setting the stage for legislative action, Eisenkot’s bloc announced it had secured the votes to install a new parliament speaker, Matan Kahana, also a former senior military figure.

But neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has the 61 votes needed to form a government.

“I am committed in this complex situation to form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible,” Eisenkot, a low-key 66-year-old who only recently entered politics, said before his swearing-in.

Netanyahu, speaking after the inaugural session, made a new push for a national-unity government, saying Israel needed to confront a threat from Iran’s clerical government, which has survived two major Israeli bombing campaigns the premier ordered with support from US President Donald Trump.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

article_html:
• Eisenkot targets Netanyahu’s legacy in first session
• Ben Gvir heckles Arab leader Yousef Jabareen during swearing-in ceremony

JERUSALEM: Tensions ran high at the first session of Israel’s parliament on Tuesday as old and new party leaders traded barbs over the possibility of forming a government with the support of Arab lists.

Two Arab parties, the Joint List and Raam, won an unprecedented 19 seats out of the parliament’s 120 in the Oct 27 election, putting them in a position of kingmakers. But in both camps, some view a government that relies on their support with deep suspicion.

During the swearing-in of the new parliament on Tuesday, far-right Israeli leader Itamar Ben Gvir heckled a prominent leader of the Arab-Israeli community.

“Who is he pledging allegiance to, Hamas?” Ben Gvir shouted at Yousef Jabareen, leader of the largest Arab-majority Joint List.

“Anyone who is not loyal shall not be in the Israeli Knesset!” (parliament) he wrote on X shortly after.

A number of lawmakers from the Joint List left the hall during the Israeli anthem, apparently to avoid standing up for it. The act of protest caused a stir in the chamber.

Netanyahu himself, in a speech during the ceremony, lamented that the two main Arab parties refuse to recognise Israel as a Jewish state — even though Raam leader Mansour Abbas has done so in the past — and claimed they sought to establish an “Islamic state” or a “nationalist Palestinian state… on the ruins of the Jewish state”.

The inauguration comes at a time of political uncertainty, with neither of the two main blocs having secured a majority. President Isaac Herzog tasked ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government on Sunday, following consultations with party leaders last week during which a majority recommended him.

Legislative onslaught

On Tuesday, Eisenkot and his allies launched a legislative onslaught against caretaker Prime Minister Netanyahu’s legacy.

Though questions still linger as to who can form a government, Eisenkot’s broad left-to-right bloc wasted no time in setting the agenda of the new Knesset with a green light from Israeli-Arab lawmakers, whose role has stirred up heated opposition from Netanyahu’s base and even right-wing supporters of Eisenkot.

Eisenkot’s Yashar party said it submitted a slew of proposals before the new parliament, including establishing an independent commission to investigate security failures that allowed the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.

Netanyahu has long opposed such a probe, denying any wrongdoing and calling instead for a politically appointed commission.

Eisenkot’s party also moved for a sweeping repeal of a judicial overhaul implemented by Netanyahu’s government, which had triggered some of Israel’s largest-ever protests before being overshadowed by three years of war.

Setting the stage for legislative action, Eisenkot’s bloc announced it had secured the votes to install a new parliament speaker, Matan Kahana, also a former senior military figure.

But neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has the 61 votes needed to form a government.

“I am committed in this complex situation to form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible,” Eisenkot, a low-key 66-year-old who only recently entered politics, said before his swearing-in.

Netanyahu, speaking after the inaugural session, made a new push for a national-unity government, saying Israel needed to confront a threat from Iran’s clerical government, which has survived two major Israeli bombing campaigns the premier ordered with support from US President Donald Trump.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Hegseth calls impeachment bid a ‘farce’
description: • Impeachment articles accuse Pentagon chief of misconduct over Iran and Yemen wars • With Trump backing, Hegseth defends military operations, says he would repeat them
author: AFP
article_text:
• Impeachment articles accuse Pentagon chief of misconduct over Iran and Yemen wars • With Trump backing, Hegseth defends military operations, says he would repeat them

WASHINGTON: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday denounced a push to impeach him as a “farce” and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under President Donald Trump.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the impeachment push “slander” and “sabotage”.

Hegseth’s combative performance came as Congress inched towards a rare vote on impeachment over alleged misconduct related to wars against Iran and Yemen’s Houthis, and the controversial killing of alleged drug smugglers in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

The effort throws down a challenge to Trump, already weakened by last week’s midterms drubbing, where anger at the sputtering Iran war and subsequent surge in fuel prices helped drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.

Trump has acknowledged that the Iran war contributed to his party losing both the House and Senate in Congress.

But moments after Hegseth’s televised press conference, the 80-year-old president signalled his backing. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

The expected vote in the House comes in the lame duck period when Republicans still retain their narrow majority, ahead of January when the huge new Democratic majority takes over.

If a majority in the House voted in favour, the Senate would still need a two-thirds majority to convict and remove Hegseth — a tall order even after Democrats take up power there too in January.

The impeachment articles have been introduced by a Republican Trump critic, Thomas Massie, who will exit Congress after losing his seat.

Trump called Massie “a disgruntled, angry, defeated former Congressman” and “a TOTAL LOSER!”

‘Would do it again’

Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers.

“I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said, also seeking to equate the effort to remove him with an attack on US troops. “These resolutions tell every one of them that their service was a crime. Their service was not a crime. These are heroes,” he said.

Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions.

Hegseth has called the widely unpopular war a “courageous and historic effort”. The 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Houthis also features in Massie’s articles of impeachment, which charge Hegseth with starting the operation without congressional approval and in the absence of an imminent threat to the US.

Massie also branded strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific as “extrajudicial killings” and said Hegseth “chilled independent legal review within the Department of Defence”.

For Hegseth, the articles of impeachment amount to an attack on Trump’s record, which he said he is happy to defend.

“If they want to talk about… President Trump’s foreign policy and national security record, let’s do it. I’ll see you there. Let’s have a conversation about the success that I outlined here,” Hegseth said.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Jemima alleges ‘violence, coercive control & abuse’ by Russell Brand
description: KARACHI: Hours after British actor Russell Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual...
author: Images Report
article_text:
KARACHI: Hours after British actor Russell Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assaults, his former partner Jemima Goldsmith publicly spoke out about the domestic abuse she allegedly suffered during their relationship.

Brand was convicted by a jury last week for one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Brand was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault. He was sentenced on Monday.

In a public statement on X, Goldsmith claimed she had her own “personal exp­e­rience of his violence, coe­rcive control and abu­se”, including a violent incident in 2014 which led her to call the police to have Brand removed from her house.

She claimed she had refrained from filing cha­rges against the comedian at the time, fearing the press attention it would bring to her and its negative impact on her children.

“Whilst my pain in relation to this pales in comparison to what the women [who] have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact,” Golds­mith continued.

“Over several years,” the producer said, “I assisted the journalists who finally exposed him … I also undertook to testify in court to his abusiveness, if the newspaper that published the victims’ accounts were ever to be sued.”

Goldsmith made clear that she is and has always been “strongly and unequivocally on the side of all of Brand’s victims”.

“I am in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand’s trial, told their stories, testified and ensured justice was done,” she said. She added that she had not been in contact with Bra­nd since 2014.

headline: White House taps Natalie Baker to be Islamabad ambassador
description: ISLAMABAD: US President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker, the current charge d’affaires at the US embassy in...
author: Dawn Report
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: US President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker, the current charge d’affaires at the US embassy in Islamabad, to be the ambassador to Pakistan, according to a statement by the White House.

“Natalie Baker, of Tex­as, a Career Member of the Senior Foreign Ser­vice, Class of Minister-Counselor, to be Amba­ssador Extraor­din­ary and Plenipotentiary of the United States of America to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan,” said a White House release regarding nominations and withdrawals.

The nomination has been submitted to the US Senate, and will be reviewed by the house foreign relations committee. If approved, the nomination will proceed to a vote by the Senate.

If confirmed, Ms Baker would be appointed the first full US ambassador to Pakistan since the departure of former envoy Donald Blome in Jan 2024.

According to her bio on the US embassy’s website, Ms Baker arrived in Islamabad as deputy chief of mission in August 2024. Earlier in her career, she also served as a consular officer in Islamabad.

Prior to her Pakistan posting, she was the deputy chief of mission at the US embassy in Doha from August 2021 to July 2024.

The Texan was also deployed as the deputy chief of mission and charge d’affaires of the US Mission to Libya, deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office at the US consulate in Dubai and economic counsellor at the embassy in Kuwait.

According to her bio, Ms Baker holds a bachelor’s degree from Princeton University and a master’s degree in public policy from the Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University.

headline: Index rallies 5,448 points on easing tensions
description: Settles above 179,000 on broad-based buying as fears of US-Iran escalation diminish
author: Muhammad Kashif
article_text:
KARACHI: The Pakis­tan Stock Exchange (PSX) maintained its northward journey on Tuesday as in­­vestors continued cherry-picking amid easing geopolitical tensions and a sharp decline in oil prices, propelling the benchmark KSE 100 index above the 179,000 level.

Brent North Sea crude, the main international benchmark, dropped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August on growing hopes of an end to the US-Iran war. Brent slid 3.1pc to $89.66 a barrel, extending sharp declines in recent trading sessions. The main US contract, West Texas Intermediate, shed 2.3pc to $84.86.

US President Donald Trump said on Monday that there was momentum towards ending the war with Iran, as he declared that the country “militarily, is effectively over”, but kept open the possibility of new strikes.

Topline Securities Ltd said the PSX witnessed a strong bullish session as the index extended its recovery following the long weekend. The index surged by 5,448.55 points, or 3.13pc, to close at 179,335.24, supported by broad-based buying across key sectors.

Settles above 179,000 on broad-based buying as fears of US-Iran escalation diminish

Investor sentiment remained upbeat amid easing international oil prices and diminishing concerns over a potential escalation in geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran. The decline in global crude oil prices further bolstered market confidence.

United Bank, Fauji Fertiliser, Hub Power, Lucky Cement and Meezan Bank emerged as the leading positive contributors, collectively adding about 1,982 points to the benchmark.

However, investor participation weakened sharply, with trading volume plunging 34.29pc to 972.4 million shares, but traded value surged 124.45pc to Rs50.7 billion from Rs22.57bn in the weekend session.

Ali Najib, Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Ltd, said the market opened on a strong note following the long weekend, surging 2,852 points to 176,739 by 9:34am, and maintained its upward momentum throughout the session. Broad-based buying supported sentiment amid easing geopolitical tensions. The index touched an intraday high of 179,424 and a low of 176,274, reflecting a wide trading range of 3,150 poi­nts, before closing firm­­ly above the 179,000 level.

On the macroeconomic front, overseas remittances increased 14pc year-on-year to $3.9bn in October.

Analysts expect the ma­­rket to consolidate betw­een 176,000 and 180,000 amid cautious sentiment ahead of the MSCI review on Wednesday. Trump peace versus strike headlines are likely to dictate near-term direction.

headline: SAI terms Rs25.30/unit ‘gross injustice’
description: KARACHI: The SITE Association of Industry (SAI) has demanded the immediate suspension of Nepra’s Incremental...
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
KARACHI: The SITE Association of Industry (SAI) has demanded the immediate suspension of Nepra’s Incremental Consumption Package, terming the revised tariff of Rs25.30 per unit a ‘gross injustice’.

SAI President Abdul Hadi said the additional cost of supplying incremental electricity was being shifted to general consumers who had not benefited from the scheme. In post-hearing comments to Nepra, the association insisted the burden must be borne exclusively by beneficiaries and not transferred through Fuel Cost Adjustments.

headline: 184 kinnow exporters get access to Uzbek market
description: De­­velopment is particularly significant given the border closures with Afgha­nis­tan, which has tradit­i­onally been a major exp­ort destination for Pakistani fruit.
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: In a maj­or development, Uzbekis­t­an’s Food Safety Commit­tee has approved 184 Pakistani kinnow exporters and 39 packhouses to access the Uzbek market.

The approval comes ahe­ad of the upcoming kinnow export season, according to an official announcement issued on Tuesday. The de­­velopment is particularly significant given the border closures with Afgha­nis­tan since October 2025.

Afghanistan has tradit­i­onally been a major exp­ort destination for Pakistani fruit, particularly kinnow and mangoes.

The approval allowed Pak­­istani kinnow exporters registered with Pakis­tan’s Department of Plant Protection (DPP), subject to fulfilling relevant regulatory and phytosanitary requirements, to access the Uzbek market.

This development is exp­ected to significantly enh­ance Pakistan’s kinnow exports and streng­then its presence in Central Asia.

The achievement refle­cts the government’s push to expand agricultural trade and follows coordinated diplomatic and technical efforts by the Minis­try of Commerce, TDAP, MNFSR, DPP, Pakistan’s Trade and Investment Counsellor in Uzbekistan, and the Embassy of Pakistan in Uzbekistan.

Pakistan appreciates the cooperation extended by the government of Uzbekistan and remains committed to strengthening bilateral trade through expanded agricultural market access, the announcement added.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Diesel rates drop, but LPG surge holds up relief for consumer
description: LPG price has shot up to Rs550 per kg; goods’ transporters reluctant to lower charges as they fear diesel prices may again start climbing.
author: Aamir Shafaat Khan
article_text:
KARACHI: The downward trend in diesel rates over the last 10 days has yet to bring any respite for the consumer because goods’ transporters are reluctant to lower charges as they fear that diesel prices may again start climbing.

Moreover, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has shot up to Rs550 per kg. The fuel is used by small vehicles for intra-city transportation of essential commodities.

The diesel rate, which was Rs402 per litre on Oct 31, has now come down to Rs378. Trailers and trucks carrying goods from Karachi to other parts of the country run on diesel.

Confusion prevails as the price of diesel, the fuel used by vehicles on long routes, has plunged, while rate for LPG, which is used by vehicles within a city, has hit the roof.

Chairman of the All Pakistan Goods Transport Alliance (APGTA) Nisar Hussain Jafri said goods carriers had discussed a move to lower freight charges, but did not act upon the suggestion because of the uncertainty surrounding daily rates determined by the government and the unpredictable Middle East conflict.

“If the government assures us that diesel prices will remain unchanged for at least 10 days, transporters may look at bringing down charges,” Mr Jafri said.

“The practice of daily revision stops us from making any long-term commitment to our clients.”

Rauf Ibrahim, a former chairman of the Karachi Wholesalers Grocers Association (KWGA), said wholesale rates had remained unchanged so far.

He said wholesalers might not pass on the impact of low transportation cost as they still have stocks of goods which they lifted at previous haulage cost.

In any diesel price fluctuation, Ibrahim added, wholesalers usually pass on the impact first, but consumers do not get any benefit as retailers either refuse to lower prices of essential items or try to buy time before doing so. In case the wholesale prices of commodities come down and retailers lift the commodities at reduced rates, he said, the city government needs to ensure that retailers pass on the impact of falling transportation charges and impose heavy fines on them if they are caught overcharging.

No change in prices

Consumers continue to pay Rs320-360 per kilogram for Masoor, Rs400-440 for Moong, Rs520-540 for Mash and Rs350-370 per kg for daal Chana, while a 20kg wheat flour bag still costs Rs2,200-3,540 despite the arrival of imported wheat last week.

Fine flour is being sold at Rs190 per kg.

A five-litre cooking oil container and a one-kilogram ghee pouch cost Rs3,090-3,115 and Rs600-640, respectively. Sugar sells at Rs140-150 per kg.

Average quality beef, with bones, is priced at Rs1,400-1,600, while boneless beef sells for Rs1,800 per kg.

The price of mutton has shot up to Rs3,000 per kg.

According to a retailer, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) plays an important role in transportation of essential goods on Suzuki and Hyundai Shehzore from Jodia Bazar and New Subzi Mandi to retail markets across the city.

“If the government assures us that diesel prices will remain unchanged for at least 10 days, transporters may look at bringing down charges,” Mr Jafri said.
“The practice of daily revision stops us from making any long-term commitment to our clients.”
Rauf Ibrahim, a former chairman of the Karachi Wholesalers Grocers Association (KWGA), said wholesale rates had remained unchanged so far.
He said wholesalers might not pass on the impact of low transportation cost as they still have stocks of goods which they lifted at previous haulage cost.

In any diesel price fluctuation, Ibrahim added, wholesalers usually pass on the impact first, but consumers do not get any benefit as retailers either refuse to lower prices of essential items or try to buy time before doing so. In case the wholesale prices of commodities come down and retailers lift the commodities at reduced rates, he said, the city government needs to ensure that retailers pass on the impact of falling transportation charges and impose heavy fines on them if they are caught overcharging.
No change in prices

Consumers continue to pay Rs320-360 per kilogram for Masoor, Rs400-440 for Moong, Rs520-540 for Mash and Rs350-370 per kg for daal Chana, while a 20kg wheat flour bag still costs Rs2,200-3,540 despite the arrival of imported wheat last week.
Fine flour is being sold at Rs190 per kg.
A five-litre cooking oil container and a one-kilogram ghee pouch cost Rs3,090-3,115 and Rs600-640, respectively. Sugar sells at Rs140-150 per kg.
Average quality beef, with bones, is priced at Rs1,400-1,600, while boneless beef sells for Rs1,800 per kg.
The price of mutton has shot up to Rs3,000 per kg.

According to a retailer, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) plays an important role in transportation of essential goods on Suzuki and Hyundai Shehzore from Jodia Bazar and New Subzi Mandi to retail markets across the city.
Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: FBR ordered to explain huge Fata tax waivers
description: Senate panel seeks consumption certificates, payments and verification documents at in-camera meeting on Nov 16.
author: Iftikhar A. Khan
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: A Senate subcommittee on Tuesday directed the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to present complete records of consumption certificates, payments and verification documents at an in-camera meeting on Nov 16.

The committee is investigating the alleged misuse of the Fata/Pata tax exemption scheme, involving imports worth Rs1,120 billion, and the recovery of evaded taxes.

The meeting of the Subcommittee of the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control was held under the chairmanship of Saifullah Abro.

At the outset, the chairman expressed serious displeasure over the absence of the Director General of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), questioning the non-serious attitude of the authorities, particularly when it had already been decided in the previous meeting that the DG would brief the committee.

Senate panel seeks consumption certificates, payments and verification documents at in-camera meeting on Nov 16

During the briefing, representatives of the FBR and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) presented their respective positions.

The FBR maintained that it had not received any formal notice from the court, whereas the FIA informed the committee that its legal adviser had received the relevant court order. The chairman and members expressed concern over the apparent lack of coordination and questioned why the FBR had remained unaware of the court proceedings for nearly two months.

The committee was briefed on the reconciliation gap between customs import data and consumption certificates for the period from 2018 to June 2026. It was informed that total imports amounted to Rs1,120.66 billion, against which consumption certificates covered imports worth Rs389.86bn, leaving an apparent unreconciled difference of Rs730.79bn.

The sector-wise analysis revealed apparent differences of Rs148.248bn in steel, Rs146.95bn in textile/fabric, Rs100.88bn in food, and Rs76.48bn in ghee and oil. The committee emphasised the need for a comprehensive, transaction-wise reconciliation to ascertain the actual position and determine any potential tax liability or revenue loss.

The FIA informed the committee that 512 notices had been issued to various companies in connection with the ongoing investigation, out of which 19 companies joined the proceedings with partial records, while more than 100 notices were returned or remained undelivered. The matter is under examination before the competent court, and proceedings are investigative in nature, aimed at obtaining relevant documents and explanations. Possible corruption, abuse of authority, diversion and wrongful release of securities are being independently examined in accordance with the law.

The chairman was also briefed about the FBR’s reluctance to share relevant records with the parliamentary committee, particularly when the department was prepared to provide information to the court and other authorities.

Referring to Article 66 of the Constitution, Mr Abro questioned the legal basis for withholding information from parliament and asked the FBR to clarify which authorities such records could be disclosed to. The members stressed that parliamentary oversight must be respected and that legal provisions should not be used to delay accountability.

The committee also examined the details of consumption certificates and payments released against them. It was observed that out of 223 companies, consumption certificates are expected to have been issued for 60 companies. The chairman sought a comprehensive explanation of the certificates, the amounts released against them and the supporting documentation.

He particularly highlighted 20 certificates involving approximately Rs64bn and directed the FBR to provide complete details, including records and justification for their issuance. He further referred to the terms of reference concerning approximately Rs74bn and questioned the release of payments without adequate verification and scrutiny.

Expressing serious concern over the financial implications, the chairman observed that the alleged tax liability associated with the matter could be substantial and that the state must recover every rupee legally due.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Development spending stalls despite surplus
description: Ministries, divisions utilise just Rs103.87bn in July-October against Rs1tr allocation.
author: Khaleeq Kiani
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The country’s Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) spending in the first four months of the current fiscal year struggled at only 10 per cent of the annual allocation.

Total PSDP spending in the first four months (July-October) of 2026-27 amounted to Rs103.87bn — 10.4pc of the Rs1trillion allocation, according to the Ministry of Planning and Development. Actual utilisation was far lower than the Rs412.3bn authorised by the Planning Commission.

This alarming spending pattern on public-interest projects, which is affecting living standards and economic growth, has emerged despite a healthy 0.8pc budget surplus posted in the first quarter of the year.

Latest data released by the Ministry of Planning and Development showed that, excluding corporations, total PSDP expenditure by about 33 ministries and divisions amounted to a meagre Rs74.65bn in the first four months, or about 11pc of the total allocation of Rs682bn. The corporations — chiefly the power sector and the National Highways Authority — together spent Rs29bn or 9.3pc against their budget allocation of Rs313bn for the whole year.

Ministries, divisions utilise just Rs103.87bn in July-October against Rs1tr allocation

The NHA could utilise only 5.8pc or Rs13.3bn in four months against its annual allocation of Rs225bn. The power sector was able to use Rs16bn or 18pc of its Rs98bn allocation. The Planning Commission had authorised disbursement of Rs78.6bn for NHA and Rs31bn to the power sector.

Under the mechanism announced by the Ministry of Finance for the current fiscal year, the government should release 15pc of budgeted allocation in the first quarter, followed by 20pc in the second quarter, 25pc in the third quarter and the remaining in the last quarter of the fiscal year to ensure that any shortfall in revenue collection is managed through cuts in the development budget to remain with fiscal targets set with the IMF.

Under this mechanism, the Planning Commission claimed that it had authorised Rs303bn for disbursement to the federal ministries in the first four months, which accounted for more than 44pc of the annual target (Rs1tr) and was higher than allowed in the finance ministry’s instructions, but only Rs75bn or 11pc, could actually be spent on the ground.

Only eight ministries were able to cross the Rs1bn spending threshold in 4MFY27, led by the Water Resources Division, which spent Rs18.7bn, or 18pc of its Rs103bn annual allocation. This was followed by Rs6.88bn expenditure in Federal Education and Professional Training against its Rs36bn allocation, accounting for 19pc. Then came Rs6.6bn spending by National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Division, achieving a healthy rate of 41pc against its allocated share of Rs16bn.

As such, NHSRC exceeded the utilisation target, which was even better when seen in the context of Rs9.6bn authorisation.

Next was Higher Education Commission with a funding utilisation of Rs4.7bn or 10pc of Rs46bn annual allocation. This was followed by the Ministry of Railways with Rs4.65bn utilisation, accounting for around 11pc of its Rs40.65bn allocation. The Ministry of Planning and Development itself used only Rs2.15bn, or less than 10pc, against its allocated share of Rs22.6bn.

After that, the Ministry of Information Technology used only Rs1.45bn or only 7.4pc of its Rs19.6bn allocation.

Combined spending in provinces and special areas (Azad Kashmir and GB) for development amounted to Rs23.8bn, or just 10pc of the annual allocation of Rs233bn and the Planning Commission’s authorisation of Rs59.8bn for the first four months. These special areas are provided funds by the finance division under a separate seasonal pattern.

Likewise, despite the country being at risk of climate disasters, the climate change division spent only Rs259 million in four months or only 10.4pc of its Rs2.5bn allocation. Another critical social-sector ministry — National Food Security — utilised less than 1.5pc (Rs65m) of its allocation of Rs4.2bn.

About six federal ministries could not spend even a single rupee for development in four months.

They included commerce, communication, Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and states and frontier regions, petroleum, privatisation, religious affairs and interfaith harmony.

ISLAMABAD: The country’s Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) spending in the first four months of the current fiscal year struggled at only 10 per cent of the annual allocation.

Total PSDP spending in the first four months (July-October) of 2026-27 amounted to Rs103.87bn — 10.4pc of the Rs1trillion allocation, according to the Ministry of Planning and Development. Actual utilisation was far lower than the Rs412.3bn authorised by the Planning Commission.

This alarming spending pattern on public-interest projects, which is affecting living standards and economic growth, has emerged despite a healthy 0.8pc budget surplus posted in the first quarter of the year.

Latest data released by the Ministry of Planning and Development showed that, excluding corporations, total PSDP expenditure by about 33 ministries and divisions amounted to a meagre Rs74.65bn in the first four months, or about 11pc of the total allocation of Rs682bn. The corporations — chiefly the power sector and the National Highways Authority — together spent Rs29bn or 9.3pc against their budget allocation of Rs313bn for the whole year.

Ministries, divisions utilise just Rs103.87bn in July-October against Rs1tr allocation

The NHA could utilise only 5.8pc or Rs13.3bn in four months against its annual allocation of Rs225bn. The power sector was able to use Rs16bn or 18pc of its Rs98bn allocation. The Planning Commission had authorised disbursement of Rs78.6bn for NHA and Rs31bn to the power sector.

Under the mechanism announced by the Ministry of Finance for the current fiscal year, the government should release 15pc of budgeted allocation in the first quarter, followed by 20pc in the second quarter, 25pc in the third quarter and the remaining in the last quarter of the fiscal year to ensure that any shortfall in revenue collection is managed through cuts in the development budget to remain with fiscal targets set with the IMF.

Under this mechanism, the Planning Commission claimed that it had authorised Rs303bn for disbursement to the federal ministries in the first four months, which accounted for more than 44pc of the annual target (Rs1tr) and was higher than allowed in the finance ministry’s instructions, but only Rs75bn or 11pc, could actually be spent on the ground.

Only eight ministries were able to cross the Rs1bn spending threshold in 4MFY27, led by the Water Resources Division, which spent Rs18.7bn, or 18pc of its Rs103bn annual allocation. This was followed by Rs6.88bn expenditure in Federal Education and Professional Training against its Rs36bn allocation, accounting for 19pc. Then came Rs6.6bn spending by National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Division, achieving a healthy rate of 41pc against its allocated share of Rs16bn.

As such, NHSRC exceeded the utilisation target, which was even better when seen in the context of Rs9.6bn authorisation.

Next was Higher Education Commission with a funding utilisation of Rs4.7bn or 10pc of Rs46bn annual allocation. This was followed by the Ministry of Railways with Rs4.65bn utilisation, accounting for around 11pc of its Rs40.65bn allocation. The Ministry of Planning and Development itself used only Rs2.15bn, or less than 10pc, against its allocated share of Rs22.6bn.

After that, the Ministry of Information Technology used only Rs1.45bn or only 7.4pc of its Rs19.6bn allocation.

Combined spending in provinces and special areas (Azad Kashmir and GB) for development amounted to Rs23.8bn, or just 10pc of the annual allocation of Rs233bn and the Planning Commission’s authorisation of Rs59.8bn for the first four months. These special areas are provided funds by the finance division under a separate seasonal pattern.

Likewise, despite the country being at risk of climate disasters, the climate change division spent only Rs259 million in four months or only 10.4pc of its Rs2.5bn allocation. Another critical social-sector ministry — National Food Security — utilised less than 1.5pc (Rs65m) of its allocation of Rs4.2bn.

About six federal ministries could not spend even a single rupee for development in four months.

They included commerce, communication, Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and states and frontier regions, petroleum, privatisation, religious affairs and interfaith harmony.

headline: Youth urged to follow Iqbal’s teachings
description: LAHORE: Veteran labour leader Khurshid Ahmad addressed a special event at the Bakhtiar Labour Hall to commemorate...
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: Veteran labour leader Khurshid Ahmad addressed a special event at the Bakhtiar Labour Hall to commemorate Iqbal Day. The event was organised under the aegis of the All Pakistan Wapda Hydro Electric Workers Union.

Mr Ahmad stated that Iqbal’s wisdom provides a timeless guide for youth and future generations to pursue hard work, self-reliance, unity, and education.

He said Iqbal played a pivotal role in awakening political, social, Islamic democratic, and fundamental rights consciousness among Muslims.

He said, “In light of Iqbal’s teachings, the youth must always stand for truth and honesty, seek knowledge, respect elders, and extend kindness to youngsters.”

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Cardiology institute facing shortage of staff and equipment
description: DERA GHAZI KHAN: The Sardar Fateh Muhammad Khan Buzdar Institute of Cardiology has been facing a shortage of staff...
author: Tariq Saeed Birmani
article_text:
DERA GHAZI KHAN: The Sardar Fateh Muhammad Khan Buzdar Institute of Cardiology has been facing a shortage of staff and equipment, requiring immediate attention to ensure the effective delivery of specialised cardiac healthcare services, Dawn has learnt.

According to official sources, among the key issues facing the hospital is the urgent need of specialist faculty, senior registrars, and essential clinical staff. The hospital is also grappling with a significant staffing shortfall, as 322 out of 686 sanctioned posts, approximately 47pc, currently lie vacant.

Sources further indicated that the provision of staff residences and hostels was also a factor for attracting qualified specialists and facilitating recruitment and retention of medical professionals.

Hospital sources further shared that on the financial front, a substantial enhancement of allocations under critical non-medicine heads were needed to meet operational requirements and ensure uninterrupted hospital functioning.

The hospital also requires the procurement and installation of essential medical equipment, including an additional cath lab, echocardiography (echo) machine, ultrasound, mobile x-ray, cardiac instrument sets, and a heart-lung machine, to strengthen diagnostic and interventional cardiac services.

Additionally, the expansion of OPD and ICU facilities is necessary to accommodate the growing patient influx, improve patient management, and enhance the overall capacity of the hospital.

Officials emphasised that strengthening human resources, ensuring adequate financial allocations, upgrading medical equipment, and expanding infrastructure are essential to make the hospital fully functional and capable of providing quality tertiary-level cardiac healthcare to the population of south Punjab and adjoining areas of Balochistan, KP and Sindh.

When contacted, Sardar Fateh Muhammad Institute of Cardiology Medical Superintendent Dr Ramzan said that his office had already requested the authorities concerned to fill the sanctioned vacant posts for the smooth running of the facility.

He further maintained that the government should advertise recruitment specifically for the Sardar Fateh Muhammad Institute of Cardiology, and it would not create additional financial burden on the government, as the finance department releases the salary budget against 686 sanctioned posts. He also mentioned the need for important equipment.

Officials emphasised that strengthening human resources, ensuring adequate financial allocations, upgrading medical equipment, and expanding infrastructure are essential to make the hospital fully functional and capable of providing quality tertiary-level cardiac healthcare to the population of south Punjab and adjoining areas of Balochistan, KP and Sindh.

When contacted, Sardar Fateh Muhammad Institute of Cardiology Medical Superintendent Dr Ramzan said that his office had already requested the authorities concerned to fill the sanctioned vacant posts for the smooth running of the facility.

He further maintained that the government should advertise recruitment specifically for the Sardar Fateh Muhammad Institute of Cardiology, and it would not create additional financial burden on the government, as the finance department releases the salary budget against 686 sanctioned posts. He also mentioned the need for important equipment.
