headline: Punjab ombudsperson seeks report on STH scams
description: After development funds scandal, irregularities surface in medicines procurement; probe finds officials guilty
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
SAHIWAL: After the development funds scam, now allegations of massive financial irregularities and misconduct have surfaced in the procurement of medicines worth more than Rs1 billion at Sahiwal Teaching Hospital (STH), where official records related to the purchases have reportedly gone ‘missing’.

Dawn learnt from sources that the regional office of the Anti-Corruption Establishment (ACE) had fixed responsibility for the recovery of Rs220 million on two former medical superintendents and pharmacist Adnan Javed.

Another Rs120m was allegedly paid to four pharmaceutical companies for medicines that were never supplied to the hospital.

After development funds scandal, irregularities surface in medicines procurement; probe finds officials guilty

Sources said Punjab Ombudsperson Ayesha Javed had sought a detailed report within 45 days on the action taken against officials held responsible for the alleged irregularities and those accused of causing a loss of Rs340m to the exchequer.

In a letter (No. 599-C0), dated Oct 9, 2026, the ACE sought the inquiry record from STH Medical Superintendent Dr Faisal Waheed.

According to the details, the inquiry originated from a complaint lodged by citizen Shahbaz Afzal in May 2026. The ACE director general subsequently referred the matter (E507/25) to the ACE Sahiwal office on Sept14, 2026.

The complaint alleged that during the procurement of medicines worth more than Rs1bn, prices were inflated by 200 to 300 per cent above approved rates before payments were made.

The inquiry reportedly held pharmacist Adnan Javed, former MS Yadullah, MS Faisal Waheed and Director Finance Abdul Aleem responsible for financial losses. It recommended the recovery of substantial amounts, including Rs120m and Rs100m from the officials concerned.

The report further alleged that four pharmaceutical companies, in collusion with hospital officials, received payments amounting to Rs120m for medicines that were never delivered to the hospital.

The matter had earlier attracted the attention of the Punjab government. On June 9, 2026, the chief minister ordered an inquiry into allegations of corruption, abuse of authority and financial irregularities in the procurement of medicines.

However, despite directions from the provincial minister and the secretary of the Specialised Healthcare and Medical Education Department, the ACE allegedly delayed action against those held responsible, even after completing its inquiry.

Following the latest developments, the Punjab ombudsperson has formally sought a report on the inquiry findings and the action taken against the officials accused of financial misconduct.

Sources further said Director Finance Abdul Aleem, who was also holding an additional charge at Sahiwal, had recently been removed from his position.

The hospital’s medical superintendent did not respond despite repeated attempts.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: PA speaker takes on Fazl, asks him hard questions
description: Says Pakistan’s involvement in Afghan war requires accountability and explanation
author: Afzal Ansari
article_text:
KASUR: Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan says JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had supported jihad during the Afghan war though the parliament had not approved it.

Later, the nation faced terrorism and other horrible consequences of the war, he said and added that past political decisions and Pakistan’s involvement in the Afghan war must be debated and that terrorism was the consequence of misguided decisions spanning over several decades.

“Difference of opinion must be countered with arguments rather than abuse and respecting the dignity and honour of Pakistan’s armed forces is a national responsibility,” he said and added that he wanted to raise several questions with Maulana Fazlur Rehman in the spirit of constructive debate.

Says Pakistan’s involvement in Afghan war requires accountability and explanation

Mr Khan was addressing the opening ceremony of phase 2 of Jashn-i-Khudian Sports Gala at Khudian Khas Sports Stadium on Tuesday.

He stressed that society needed new ideas and intellectual perspectives as the absence of fresh thinking would only compound existing challenges.

He added that disruptions and disorder in legislative assemblies were increasingly leaving little room for meaningful debate on Allama Iqbal’s concept of a new world.

“What was the practical form of the new world envisioned by Allama Iqbal? Which parliament had authorised Pakistan’s involvement in the Afghan war following the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan? In which parliamentary forum had decisions regarding the Mujahideen and the then US administration been taken?”

The speaker said decisions had been made to involve Pakistan in wars without obtaining parliamentary approval and their consequences continued to haunt successive generations in the form of fear, terrorism and insecurity.

He suggested that Pakistan’s involvement in the Afghan war, subsequent policies and political decisions taken during different periods required accountability and explanation through reasoned debate.

Referring to the devastating impact of terrorism, he said schools, colleges, markets, public squares, courts, the armed forces and police personnel had all been targeted.

The question was what kind of intellectual thinking had allowed terrorism to take root in society and disrupt the everyday lives of ordinary citizens, said Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan.

Coming back to the subject of Maulana Fazlur Rehman, he suggested to him to explain, through reasoned argument, the past political decisions concerning the Legal Framework Order, election of a uniformed president, the Hasba Bill, formation of the Muttahida Majlis-i-Amal (MMA) and the 2002 general elections.

The PA speaker said forceful rhetoric alone could not establish one’s preferred position as correct or dismiss an opposing viewpoint as wrong and difference of opinion should be answered with arguments rather than abuse, intimidation, threats or ridicule.

Speaking about the security situation, he said terrorism was the consequence of misguided decisions taken over several decades and it had now become a grave challenge, threatening both human lives and the country’s national ideology.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: UET convocation ‘Engineering fundamental pillar of national development’
description: LAHORE: As many as 2,957 students were awarded degrees at the 33rd annual convocation of the University of...
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: As many as 2,957 students were awarded degrees at the 33rd annual convocation of the University of Engineering and Technology (UET) on Tuesday.

Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal was the chief guest and the High Commissioner of Bangladesh, HE Muhammad Iqbal Hussain Khan, Deputy High Commissioner Fazal Lohani Babu, and other distinguished diplomatic, academic and administrative personalities also attended the ceremony.

Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Shahid Munir presided over the convocation as chancellor under the powers delegated by the governor.

Addressing the convocation, Mr Iqbal said that UET would be transformed into one of Pakistan’s leading research centres through the establishment of centres of excellence and state-of-the-art laboratories.

He said engineering education was a fundamental pillar of national development and UET graduates had consistently played a significant role in Pakistan’s progress.

Highlighting the importance of political stability for sustainable economic growth and investment, Mr Iqbal said investors preferred economies offering peace, stability and continuity of policies. He proposed a political charter for the next 10 years, urging political forces to resolve differences within constitutional and democratic parameters.

Prof Munir requested an increase in the university’s budget to facilitate the completion of ongoing development projects and the launch of new research initiatives.

Highlighting UET’s achievements over the past two years, he said that UET Lahore had secured 201st position globally in engineering and technology in the QS rankings, 192nd in the Asian University Rankings and 603rd in the QS Sustainability Ranking.

He said the university’s annual budget had increased from Rs5.4 billion to Rs8.5 billion, with approximately 70pc of its financial requirements being generated through its own resources. He further stated that scholarships worth Rs1.4 billion were being provided to approximately 9,000 students during the current year. Over the past two years, student enrolment had doubled from 12,500 to 25,000, while 64 new academic programmes had also been introduced. The graduating class included 22 international students, he said.

Addressing the graduating students, Prof Munir urged young graduates to embrace artificial intelligence, entrepreneurship and emerging technologies to help transform Pakistan into a knowledge-based economy.

Students from UET’s main campus Lahore and its campuses in Kala Shah Kaku, Faisalabad, Narowal and Gujranwala received degrees.

headline: PMML seeks CM’s apology
description: LAHORE: Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) President Khalid Masood Sindhu on Tuesday demanded an apology from...
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) President Khalid Masood Sindhu on Tuesday demanded an apology from Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz over what he termed baseless allegations against his party following the NA-77 by-election in Gujranwala by her and her cabinet member.

He warned that the party would be entitled to initiate action against her at every available forum if she failed to do so.

Sindhu said the people knew that the PMML had won the by-election, but the PML-N manipulated the results by using ministers, members of the national and provincial assemblies, polling staff and police personnel.

“Rather than answering the questions raised about the election, the chief minister has made baseless allegations against our party. This reflects political panic and a lack of public support,” he said.

Maryam Nawaz in a post on X said: “In Gujranwala, all the major rival groups, including the banned organisations and the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI), contested the election under a new name against PML-N. Yet, despite joining hands, they suffered a humiliating defeat.”

Similarly, Punjab Information and Culture Minister Azma Bokhari criticised the PMML, questioning “how organisations declared proscribed by the state could change their names and openly participate in political activities.” Bokhari termed the participation of PMML in politics a major challenge to the state.

“We urge the Election Commission of Pakistan to take notice as how can organisations supported by terrorists openly engage in political activities?” she questioned.

headline: Ajoka moves to cinema with biopic on Bali Jatti
description: LAHORE: After decades of contributing to theatre, Ajoka is taking its creative journey from stage to screen with its...
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: After decades of contributing to theatre, Ajoka is taking its creative journey from stage to screen with its first feature film, Bali Jatti, based on the life and struggles of legendary Punjabi folk theatre performer Bali Jatti.

Ajoka Productions unveiled the film’s logo, teaser and a song at a launch event in Lahore.

Written, researched and directed by Shahid Nadeem, founder and executive director of Ajoka Theatre, the film will revisit the cultural landscape of 1970s Punjab, highlighting its folk music, theatrical traditions and the golden era of Punjabi theatre.

The film traces the journey of Bali Jatti, whose real name was Inayat Bibi, from a young singer facing family and social opposition to becoming a prominent figure in folk theatre. It will explore her artistic struggles, personal relationships, professional rivalries and the challenges she encountered throughout her career.

Speaking at the launch, Shahid Nadeem said the film is an effort to bring the remarkable story of an important figure in Punjab’s folk theatre history to the cinema screen and introduce her legacy to a wider audience.

Renowned folk singer Arif Lohar appreciated Ajoka’s initiative, saying that the film would help revive memories of the golden era of Punjabi folk theatre, associated with celebrated performers such as Bali Jatti and Alam Lohar etc. Dr Fozia Saeed, former director general of the Pakistan National Council of the Arts, shared insights from her research on Bali Jatti and highlighted the importance of documenting the life and artistic contributions of the legendary performer.

Those present at the event included folk artist Abbas Jatt, photographer and stylist Khawar Riaz, PILAC Director General Aslam Shahid, fashion designer Mehmood Bhatti, Ajoka Institute Director Nirvaan Nadeem, Ajoka Chair Zara Salman and television producer Mohsin Jaffar, among others.

Casting for the film is currently underway. Shooting is planned in Lahore and its surrounding areas, with production targeting completion by March. The film is planned for an initial release in Pakistani cinemas, followed by international and OTT distribution.

With Bali Jatti, Ajoka Productions aims to bring an important chapter of Punjab’s folk.

headline: Poor air quality not linked to Diwali fireworks in India: report
description: PAQI says Lahore’s PM2.5 level eight times WHO guideline
author: Imran Gabol
article_text:
LAHORE: Satellite data detected 16,714 farm fires in Punjab between Oct 1 and Nov 9 while Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration was eight times the World Health Organisation’s guideline value, according to a report by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI) that questioned the link between Diwali fireworks in India and the city’s pollution.

The report, released on Tuesday, said the number of likely farm fires in Punjab, Pakistan, remained almost unchanged from the corresponding period last year.

Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration stood at 126 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, exceeding the 24-hour National Environmental Quality Standards (NEQS) on all 40 days for which valid data were available. The average was 11pc lower than in the corresponding period in 2025.

Satellite instruments detected 18,825 fires across Punjab, Pakistan, 89pc of which were classified as likely crop-residue burning. The highest daily count was recorded on Nov 1, with 1,102 detections.

PAQI says Lahore’s PM2.5 level eight times WHO guideline

Sheikhupura recorded the highest number of fires at 2,559, followed by Jhang (2,192), Okara (2,062), Hafizabad (1,893) and Gujranwala (1,417). The five districts accounted for 54pc of the total detections.

The report found a positive correlation between upwind fire activity and PM2.5 levels in Lahore. On days when air trajectories passed over areas where burning was taking place, the average concentration reached 175 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with 93 micrograms on other days.

A similar pattern was observed in Multan, where average PM2.5 levels reached 203 micrograms on days influenced by fires, compared with 88 micrograms on other days.

In Bahawalpur, the corresponding figures were 125 and 65 micrograms.

However, the report cautioned that the association did not establish the precise contribution of crop-residue burning to urban pollution as stagnant weather conditions and reduced atmospheric dispersion also contributed to the accumulation of pollutants.

The number of likely crop-residue fires in Punjab, Pakistan, was 8pc above the 2020-2025 average, although the comparable satellite record showed a 1pc decline from 2025.

The assessment also examined whether fireworks during Diwali celebrations in India on Nov 8 had contributed to deteriorating air quality in Punjab. It found that easterly winds carried air from Indian territory towards Pakistan during the night. Of the 48 back trajectories arriving in Lahore, Kasur and Sialkot between 9pm on Nov 8 and midnight on Nov 10, 45 had passed over Indian territory within the preceding 12 hours, most frequently near Tarn Taran, Amritsar and Jammu. However, the report said the available evidence did not support attributing Lahore’s poor air quality after Diwali to fireworks across the border.

Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration between 6pm on Nov 8 and 1am on Nov 10 was 234 micrograms per cubic metre, 10pc higher than the average recorded during the same hours over the preceding seven days.

In comparison, the average concentration in Kasur increased by 27pc and in Sialkot by 33pc, while Narowal recorded a 2pc decline.

The increase was greater in cities farther from the international border. Faisalabad, located 130km from the border, recorded a 40pc increase, while Multan, 180km away, also saw a 40pc rise. The average increase in the four border cities — Lahore, Kasur, Sialkot and Narowal — was 36 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with 85 micrograms in Faisalabad and Multan.

The report noted that pollution transported from across the border would be expected to cause a greater increase in border areas than in cities farther inland. However, the observed pattern did not support that explanation. Sialkot was an exception, recording a 37pc increase in PM2.5 during the night after Diwali, with air trajectories passing over the Jammu area.

The assessment also found that emissions from New Delhi had not reached Lahore during the period analysed. Air from Delhi entered Pakistan near Rahim Yar Khan and Bahawalpur only after 3am on Nov 10, with its closest approach to Lahore remaining 266 kilometres away.

The report said distinguishing between emissions from fireworks and smoke from agricultural fires required chemical analysis of particulate matter, including elements such as potassium, strontium and barium, which Pakistani monitoring stations did not measure.

Meanwhile, due to smog and bad air quality in Lahore, the second Test match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, scheduled to be played in Lahore from Nov 17 to 21, has been shifted to Rawalpindi, according to the Pakistan Cricket Board.

On the other hand, the Punjab Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EPCCD) reported an improvement in Lahore’s air quality on Monday following emergency mitigation and enforcement operations.

The city’s average air quality index (AQI) reading, recorded at 489 at 9am, fell to 232 by 3pm — a reduction of 257 points, or approximately 53pc — according to the department’s monitoring network.

Data from all 11 monitoring stations showed a decline in AQI readings during the period. Egerton Road recorded the biggest improvement, with its reading falling from 500 to 167, followed by GT Road, where the AQI dropped from 500 to 172. DHA Phase 6, Shahdara, Barki Road and Punjab University also recorded improvements, as did Wagah Border, Gulberg III, Kahna Nau, Safari Park and Multan Road.EPCCD Secretary Silwat Saeed said the department was responding to deteriorating air quality through coordinated enforcement, real-time environmental monitoring and targeted field interventions. She said the department was using its monitoring infrastructure and Punjab Climate Watch data to identify pollution hotspots and direct operational teams to areas requiring immediate action.

Environment Protection Agency (EPA) Director General Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh said the department had adopted a zero-tolerance approach towards major sources of air pollution.The PAQI report indicated a very high number of fires in areas upwind of Lahore on Nov 10, 11 and 12, with 642, 668 and 617 fires, respectively, expected under forecast wind conditions.

Separately, the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) on Tuesday forecast rain in most districts of Punjab over the next two days, saying it was likely to reduce smog but intensify cold weather.

According to a PDMA alert issued on Tuesday, Lahore, Kasur, Sialkot, Narowal, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Sheikhupura, Khushab, Bhakkar and Sargodha are among the districts likely to receive rainfall.

The report said distinguishing between emissions from fireworks and smoke from agricultural fires required chemical analysis of particulate matter, including elements such as potassium, strontium and barium, which Pakistani monitoring stations did not measure.

Meanwhile, due to smog and bad air quality in Lahore, the second Test match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, scheduled to be played in Lahore from Nov 17 to 21, has been shifted to Rawalpindi, according to the Pakistan Cricket Board.

On the other hand, the Punjab Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EPCCD) reported an improvement in Lahore’s air quality on Monday following emergency mitigation and enforcement operations.

The city’s average air quality index (AQI) reading, recorded at 489 at 9am, fell to 232 by 3pm — a reduction of 257 points, or approximately 53pc — according to the department’s monitoring network.

Data from all 11 monitoring stations showed a decline in AQI readings during the period. Egerton Road recorded the biggest improvement, with its reading falling from 500 to 167, followed by GT Road, where the AQI dropped from 500 to 172. She said the department was using its monitoring infrastructure and Punjab Climate Watch data to identify pollution hotspots and direct operational teams to areas requiring immediate action.

Environment Protection Agency (EPA) Director General Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh said the department had adopted a zero-tolerance approach towards major sources of air pollution.The PAQI report indicated a very high number of fires in areas upwind of Lahore on Nov 10, 11 and 12, with 642, 668 and 617 fires, respectively, expected under forecast wind conditions.

Separately, the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) on Tuesday forecast rain in most districts of Punjab over the next two days, saying it was likely to reduce smog but intensify cold weather.

According to a PDMA alert issued on Tuesday, Lahore, Kasur, Sialkot, Narowal, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Sheikhupura, Khushab, Bhakkar and Sargodha are among the districts likely to receive rainfall.

headline: Sugarcane growers threaten to burn crops
description: LAHORE: Calling for an immediate agricultural emergency, Pakistan Kissan Ittehad President Khalid Mahmood Khokhar...
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: Calling for an immediate agricultural emergency, Pakistan Kissan Ittehad President Khalid Mahmood Khokhar lashed out at the government for its “total indifference” toward sugarcane growers, warning that farmers will burn their crops if a coherent policy and sugarcane crushing schedule are not announced at once.

Addressing a press conference here on Tuesday, he said that despite sugarcane cultivation expanding by 16pc compared to the last year, spanning over 2.45 million acres in Punjab alone, the authorities had failed to announce either a crushing season start date or a minimum support price.

“The government was quick to declare dates for the Basant festival, yet it remains completely silent on the sugarcane crushing schedule and support price,” he lamented.

He highlighted the mounting financial distress of the farming community, pointing out that while open-market wheat prices hovered around Rs5,500 per maund, sugarcane growers were denied even basic cost calculations.

Based on current production expenses, Mr Khokhar stated, the fair minimum price for sugarcane stands at Rs700 per maund.

“We do not beg for subsidies; we demand fair returns for our hard work,” he emphasised, noting that Pakistani farmers face higher input costs than growers anywhere else in the world. He added that essential inputs like urea were being openly sold at a black-market premium of Rs400 to Rs500 per bag.

Decrying the lack of a long-term agricultural vision, Mr Khokhar regretted that a country once renowned for exporting cotton was now forced to import its entire requirement. He urged the higher authorities and policymakers to intervene immediately to end step-motherly treatment of the agrarian sector and save growers from complete financial ruin.

headline: Qureshi moved to PIC days after he collapsed in jail, alleges lawyer
description: Says the PTI leader is under medical observation for 24 hours to decide if he needs hospital admission
author: Mansoor Malik
article_text:
LAHORE: The lawyer representing Shah Mahmood Qureshi said on Tuesday that the senior PTI leader, who is currently incarcerated at Kot Lakhpat jail, was taken to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) days after suffering a fall.

Qureshi has been indicted in multiple cases pertaining to theMay 9, 2023 riots and has remained behind bars since August 2023. In July 2024, the PTI leader was indicted by a Lahore antiterrorism court in a case registered by the Shadman police on the charges of attacking and burning the police station.

Speaking to Dawn, his counsel Rana Mudassar Umar said: “[Qureshi] was taken to the PIC today (Tuesday) as he fainted and suffered a fall a few days ago. We had submitted an application in the antiterrorism court; however, due to holidays, the issue was delayed.”

He said that Qureshi was being held under observation for 24 hours, “after which it will be decided whether he has to be admitted to the hospital.”

Says the PTI leader is under medical observation for 24 hours to decide if he needs hospital admission

Last week, Qureshi’s daughter, Meher Bano, in a post on social media platform X, had said that she had learnt about her father’s fall from “family after they met him in Kot Lakhpat jail.”

“Three-and-a-half years ago a hale and hearty lion heart was sent to jail on trumped up charges … For over two years, he has been in Kot Lakhpat jail now facing ludicrous and false charges relating to May 9. He has been acquitted multiple times but [remains] behind bars due to the government’s mala fide,” she alleged.

Qureshi’s son, Zain, said on Wednesday that he met his father in jail, where he mentioned that he had collapsed while walking within his barracks. “I request the prison authorities to immediately arrange for a CT scan so that his [Qureshi’s] health condition can be thoroughly assessed.

Furthermore, he should be taken to a qualified dentist for the treatment of a cracked tooth,” he said on X.

On Nov 6, a meeting of the PTI core committee also expressed concern over Qureshi’s “fall and the resulting impact on his health.”

The committee demanded the relevant courts, the government and the prison administration immediately transfer Qureshi to a hospital and ensure his complete medical examination and necessary treatment.

In December last year, Qureshi, who is also a former foreign minister, underwent a procedure to get his gallbladder removed at the Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute. Prior to that, he was taken to the PIC in May after complaining of heart pain.

headline: Eight indicted in foreign women’s rape case
description: Judge directs prosecution to present its witnesses on Dec 9 so the formal trial proceedings could be commenced.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: A sessions court on Tuesday indicted eight suspects, including one reportedly linked to a senior minister, in a case of alleged gang rape of two foreign women.

All the suspects, presently in judicial custody, were produced before the trial court for the indictment proceedings.

Additional District & Sessions Judge (AD&SJ) Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed the charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty.

The judge directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on Dec 9 so the formal trial proceedings could be commenced.

Separately, the judge gave the last opportunity to the prosecution to present its arguments on the post-arrest bail petitions of three of the suspects in the case.

The judge observed that the prosecution had availed multiple opportunities to argue the bail petitions on one pretext or the other.

The judge adjourned the bail hearing till Nov 11 (today) with a clear warning to the prosecution to present its arguments, otherwise, the petitions would be decided in light of the case record.

Advocate Salman Shahid had already concluded his arguments on behalf of the petitioners/suspects.

Defence-C police in its challan (investigation report) had cleared five suspects, including the one linked to the senior political figure, of sexual assault charges and implicated them in minor offences of illegal detention and extortion.

The police charged three other suspects, who were allegedly low-paid employees of one of the key suspects, with sexually assaulting the women.

headline: Millers demand market-driven wheat policy, targeted subsidy
description: Urge govt to replace untargeted flour subsidies with direct financial assistance to low-income households to eliminate severe market distortions.
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: The Progressive group of the Pakistan Flour Mills Association (PFMA) has urged the government to adopt a market-driven wheat policy and replace untargeted flour subsidies with direct financial assistance to low-income households to eliminate severe market distortions.

Frequent shifts in government policy – ranging from rationing and quota systems to varying procurement arrangements – have bred uncertainty, undermining both farmers and mill owners, progressive miller Khaleeq Arshad told reporters here on Tuesday.

Recalling market trends, he noted that flour bag prices once dropped from Rs2,800 to Rs1,300 purely due to improved supply and healthy competition, rather than state intervention. Conversely, when prices naturally rose, the government imposed artificial price caps and targeted millers for price manipulation, ignoring that higher prices incentivised farmers to increase wheat cultivation in subsequent seasons. While acknowledging the fixing of the wheat support price at Rs4,500 per maund as a positive step for growers, Mr Arshad emphasised that wheat releases to flour mills must reflect actual procurement, storage, and transport expenses.

“Procuring wheat at Rs4,500 per maund and subsequently releasing it at a substantially lower price creates deep distortions in the market and leads to severe operational problems,” he observed.

Instead of blanket flour subsidies that equally benefit affluent consumers and low-income groups, he recommended leveraging existing social safety nets such as the Benazir Income Support Programme, Kissan Card, and Punjab government initiatives to deliver direct financial relief to underprivileged households.

He also called for maintaining strategic wheat reserves strictly to manage emergency shortages rather than to artificially suppress prices, adding that any emergency releases should occur at prevailing market rates.

Addressing structural flaws in mill quotas, the PFMA leader questioned the ongoing allocation of wheat to inactive units, asserting that the state holds no obligation to keep commercially unviable operations afloat. Quotas, he argued, should be allocated to active mills based strictly on performance and open competition.

He criticised the government’s dual approach of partially liberalising the market while retaining heavy-handed controls on prices and supplies, urging policymakers to choose a definitive direction. Highlighting current operational losses, he pointed out that while subsidised wheat is released at around Rs3,700 per maund against market rates of roughly Rs5,400 per maund, mills are being forced to sell 20 to 25 per cent of flour produced from their own commercially bought, expensive wheat at the lower subsidised rates.

Urging an immediate end to this requirement, he stated that mills should supply subsidised flour strictly in proportion to the subsidised grain provided to them.

headline: Sustained psychological support stressed for school collapse survivors
description: PESHAWAR: Experts have called for four to six weeks of sustained psychological support for survivors and families of...
author: Bureau Report
article_text:
PESHAWAR: Experts have called for four to six weeks of sustained psychological support for survivors and families of the 31 children killed in the recent roof collapse at a private school in Peshawar, warning that those affected would need continued counselling to cope with the trauma of the tragedy.

They also stressed the urgent need for comprehensive psychological assessments and trauma-focused interventions for the two most severely affected children.

They were speaking during a medical camp organised by the Khyber Association of Clinical Psychologists (KACP) in collaboration with Syed Sultan Psychiatric Hospital here the other day.

The activity was meant to provide psychological support, human connection and a safe beginning to the healing process of the survivors of the tragedy.

On the occasion, KACP co-founder Prof Erum Irshad said structured bereavement support for families who had lost children was among the urgent interventions required, alongside psychological first-aid training for school staff.

She also called for the long-term integration of mental health services into school disaster preparedness and response plans across the province.

The camp identified psychological distress among children and their families through activities that did not require them to recount their traumatic experiences.

Ms Irshad, who is a former chairperson of the department of psychology at the University of Peshawar, said they understood that children did not need another reminder of what had happened but rather an environment where they could feel safe without being pressured to speak.

Instead of asking children to describe their traumatic experiences, psychologists engaged them in creative activities, in line with the principles of psychological first aid, which emphasise safety, calm, connection, self-efficacy and hope, she said.

She said international guidelines also caution against forcing survivors to recount traumatic experiences through psychological debriefing. “The team believed that healing should begin with trust, not interrogation.”

Ms Irshad said beyond the investigation and its findings, the deepest consequences of the tragedy were being borne by the families, children and teachers who had to continue living in its aftermath.

Dr Mehwish Sultan of Syed Sultan Psychiatric Hospital said children did not need to relive the worst day of their lives in front of strangers. “What they needed first was a safe adult, a predictable environment and the freedom to express themselves in their own way.”

She said the survivors had witnessed horrific scenes and were likely to experience psychological distress, making comprehensive psychological assessments and appropriate interventions essential.

KACP’s Dr Saira Ayub said one household had lost four children. She said the activities organised by the team formed the heart of the children’s programme. These included ‘Feelings Through Colours’, ‘Emotional Weather’, ‘Safe or Comforting Place’, ‘Growing Tree’, ‘Garden of Hope’ and ‘Helping Hands’, as well as free drawing, colouring, pasting and collage-making.

PESHAWAR: Experts have called for four to six weeks of sustained psychological support for survivors and families of the 31 children killed in the recent roof collapse at a private school in Peshawar, warning that those affected would need continued counselling to cope with the trauma of the tragedy.

They also stressed the urgent need for comprehensive psychological assessments and trauma-focused interventions for the two most severely affected children.

They were speaking during a medical camp organised by the Khyber Association of Clinical Psychologists (KACP) in collaboration with Syed Sultan Psychiatric Hospital here the other day.

The activity was meant to provide psychological support, human connection and a safe beginning to the healing process of the survivors of the tragedy.

On the occasion, KACP co-founder Prof Erum Irshad said structured bereavement support for families who had lost children was among the urgent interventions required, alongside psychological first-aid training for school staff.

She also called for the long-term integration of mental health services into school disaster preparedness and response plans across the province.

The camp identified psychological distress among children and their families through activities that did not require them to recount their traumatic experiences.

Ms Irshad, who is a former chairperson of the department of psychology at the University of Peshawar, said they understood that children did not need another reminder of what had happened but rather an environment where they could feel safe without being pressured to speak.

Instead of asking children to describe their traumatic experiences, psychologists engaged them in creative activities, in line with the principles of psychological first aid, which emphasise safety, calm, connection, self-efficacy and hope, she said.

She said international guidelines also caution against forcing survivors to recount traumatic experiences through psychological debriefing. “The team believed that healing should begin with trust, not interrogation.”

Ms Irshad said beyond the investigation and its findings, the deepest consequences of the tragedy were being borne by the families, children and teachers who had to continue living in its aftermath.

Dr Mehwish Sultan of Syed Sultan Psychiatric Hospital said children did not need to relive the worst day of their lives in front of strangers. “What they needed first was a safe adult, a predictable environment and the freedom to express themselves in their own way.”

She said the survivors had witnessed horrific scenes and were likely to experience psychological distress, making comprehensive psychological assessments and appropriate interventions essential.

KACP’s Dr Saira Ayub said one household had lost four children. She said the activities organised by the team formed the heart of the children’s programme. These included ‘Feelings Through Colours’, ‘Emotional Weather’, ‘Safe or Comforting Place’, ‘Growing Tree’, ‘Garden of Hope’ and ‘Helping Hands’, as well as free drawing, colouring, pasting and collage-making.

headline: ATC refuses to drop terror charges in PAF officer murder case
description: ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Tuesday rejected a defence plea seeking the removal of terrorism-related...
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Tuesday rejected a defence plea seeking the removal of terrorism-related charges from the murder case of late Group Captain Asim Tariq, ruling that the trial would continue before the anti-terrorism court.

ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Mohammad Zulqarnain announced the decision after hearing arguments from the defence counsel and prosecutor.

During the proceedings, the defence counsel argued that the provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act were not applicable to the case and requested the court to decide the matter before recording statements of prosecution witnesses.

However, the prosecutor opposed the plea, arguing that the nature and circumstances of the incident warranted the inclusion of terrorism charges. He maintained that the court could proceed with recording prosecution witnesses’ statements in light of precedents set by higher courts.

The prosecutor further argued that if the court found at any stage of the trial that the terrorism provisions were not applicable, it had the authority to transfer the case to the appropriate forum. He said it was premature to question the applicability of the charges as no prosecution witness had yet been examined.

The judge initially reserved the decision on the defence application and took a brief recess. After resuming the proceedings, he dismissed the plea and directed that the trial proceed before the ATC.

The court subsequently summoned prosecution witnesses and adjourned further proceedings until Wednesday (today). Police had registered the murder case against the accused at Margalla Police Station.

headline: Jirga opposes relocation of bus terminal from Tank city
description: APPBy Our Correspondent DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A jirga on Tuesday opposed the proposed relocation of the Tank bus...
author: APP
article_text:
APPBy Our Correspondent

DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A jirga on Tuesday opposed the proposed relocation of the Tank bus terminal from the city and formed a committee to take up the issue with the relevant authorities.

The jirga was held at the District Press Club Tank, with office-bearers of the transporters’ union, local elders and other residents in attendance.

Speaking at the jirga, Malik Pato Bittani, Saddam Hussain Bittani, Iftikhar Bittani, Pir Saleem Shah, Sheikh Naseer, Naik Badshah and others said they would not allow the bus terminal to be shifted outside the city.

They argued that relocating the terminal outside the city amid the prevailing precarious law and order situation could put people’s lives at risk.

The speakers also cautioned that decisions such as relocation of the terminal could fuel resentment among residents towards the state and urged the government to take ground realities and public difficulties into consideration.

They said they did not want to resort to confrontation or protests and wanted to resolve the issue through dialogue.

The participants also expressed concern over the absence of development council members from the jirga and called upon all relevant representatives to play their role in resolving the issue.

BLAST DAMAGES BRIDGE: A powerful explosion damaged a bridge and the adjoining road in the Pathankot area of Tank district, triggering panic among residents, police sources said on Tuesday.

According to them, the explosion occurred beneath a bridge on the main Peshawar Road on the outskirts of Tank city on Monday night. No casualties were reported.

The intensity of the blast damaged the bridge and sections of the adjoining road, while solar panels installed on the roofs of nearby houses were also damaged.

Residents said pieces of what appeared to be human remains were found at the site, raising speculation that a person involved in planting the explosive material may have been caught in the blast.

However, there was no official confirmation about the identity or origin of the remains, or whether any person was involved in planting the explosives.

Authorities have begun collecting information about the nature of the explosion, the material used and the possible involvement of any individuals or groups.

description: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court has issued a notice to the attorney general for Pakistan, seeking his response to...
author: Bureau Report
article_text:
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court has issued a notice to the attorney general for Pakistan, seeking his response to a petition challenging legality of the imposition of property tax by cantonment boards and the relevant provisions of the law in this regard.

A bench consisting of Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Babar Sattar also sought comments within a fortnight from the respondents, including the defence secretary, director general and additional director general of Military Lands and Cantonments Department, Rawalpindi, chief executive officer of Peshawar Cantonment Board and secretary of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa excise and taxation department.

It issued the notice to the attorney general for Pakistan under Order XXVII-A of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, observing that constitutional vires and interpretation of Section 60 of the Cantonments Act, 1924, are involved in the matter.

The petitioners, including Mian Mohammad Tariq Siddiqui and several other citizens, requested the court to declare unconstitutional and without lawful authority the imposition, assessment and collection of tax on annual rental value (ARV) of immovable properties by the respondents.

They said that the imposition of the impugned tax should be declared beyond the legislative competence of the federation under Entry 50 in Part I of the Federal Legislative List, which expressly excluded taxes on immovable properties, and also to quash the impugned assessment notices, demands and recovery proceedings against the petitioners.

Advocate Hafiz Zain Rasheed appeared for the petitioners and contended that Section 60 of the Cantonments Act, 1924, as substituted through the Cantonments (Amendment) Act, 2023, read with Schedule VII (a), which provided for taxation on the annual rental value of immovable property was in conflict with the constitutional scheme as property taxes on immovable properties could only be imposed and levied by provinces as it was a provincial subject under the Constitution.

He argued that the impugned taxation framework was inconsistent with the constitutional distribution of legislative powers following the enactment of the Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, particularly in view of Entry 50 of the Federal Legislative List, and the provincial legislative framework governing taxation of immovable property.

The lawyer questioned the constitutional validity and continued applicability of Presidential Order No 13 of 1979, promulgated during the Gen Ziaul Haq rule in 1979 and sought a declaration that the order in question can’t sustain the impugned taxation framework insofar as it is in conflict with the constitutional scheme following the Eighteenth Amendment.

He argued that the restoration and restructuring of the constitutional distribution of legislative powers through subsequent constitutional amendments could not be overridden by a presidential order and that the authority to impose taxes must be traceable to a valid constitutional and legislative source.

Mr Rasheed questioned the substantial enhancement of annual rental values of commercial properties located within the Peshawar cantonment area, including Saddar Bazaar, Shoba Bazaar and Khyber Bazaar, and alleged a 200-300 per cent increase compared to previous property taxes.

He maintained that the impugned assessments violated statutory safeguards and principles of natural justice, while also raising questions concerning the applicability of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958, to properties situated within cantonment areas.

The counsel said imposition and collection of property taxes within provinces was a provincial subject and the KP government was constitutionally competent to levy property tax even within the areas of Peshawar’s cantonment board area through the excise and taxation department.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Drive against cervical cancer begins in Chitral today
description: CHITRAL: A comprehensive 15-day vaccination campaign targeting cervical cancer is scheduled to be launched across...
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
CHITRAL: A comprehensive 15-day vaccination campaign targeting cervical cancer is scheduled to be launched across Lower Chitral from today (November 11) to November 25, health authorities announced.

The mega-drive aims to vaccinate 22,000 girls aged between 9 and 15 to protect them against the deadly disease. Briefing the media at Chitral Press Club, Deputy District Health Officer Dr Irshad Ahmed and Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) District Coordinator Dr Farman Nizar Khan shared the strategic blueprint of the campaign.

To ensure 100 per cent coverage, the Health Department has constituted 26 specialised mobile teams across the district. These teams will systematically cover all government and private schools, as well as religious seminaries, which collectively account for approximately 95 per cent of the enrolled target population. Simultaneously, an intensive door-to-door campaign will be conducted to identify and reach out-of-school girls and those missed during institutional visits, ensuring that no child is left unprotected.

Health officials highlighted that the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine has now been formally integrated into Pakistan’s national EPI network as the 14th vaccine-preventable disease and this specific drive focuses on girls over 9 years old who have not yet received the injection.

Warning of the severity of the illness, the medical experts noted that cervical cancer ranks as the third most prevalent and fatal cancer among women worldwide, claiming millions of lives annually while developed nations initiated mass vaccination as early as 1995, Pakistan formally launched its national rollout in 2025.

Addressing scepticism and misinformation circulating on social media, health officials categorically dismissed concerns regarding the vaccine’s safety and religious permissibility.

They clarified that Islamic countries, including Saudi Arabia, incorporated the vaccine into their national healthcare frameworks as early as 2010. They further stated that leading Islamic scholars and religious authorities, both internationally and within Pakistan, had reviewed its medical credentials and issued formal religious rulings (fatwas) declaring it permissible (halal).

The administration urged parents, educators and members of civil society to extend their full cooperation to the visiting vaccination teams and play an active role in ensuring the campaign’s success.

Officials also highlighted the vaccine’s high cost in the private market, where a single dose can cost up to Rs42,000, placing it beyond the financial reach of many ordinary citizens. They emphasised that the government is making this potentially life-saving vaccine available completely free of charge, providing an important opportunity to protect children without placing a financial burden on families.

They clarified that Islamic countries, including Saudi Arabia, incorporated the vaccine into their national healthcare frameworks as early as 2010. They further stated that leading Islamic scholars and religious authorities, both internationally and within Pakistan, had reviewed its medical credentials and issued formal religious rulings (fatwas) declaring it permissible (halal).
The administration urged parents, educators and members of civil society to extend their full cooperation to the visiting vaccination teams and play an active role in ensuring the campaign’s success.

Officials also highlighted the vaccine’s high cost in the private market, where a single dose can cost up to Rs42,000, placing it beyond the financial reach of many ordinary citizens. They emphasised that the government is making this potentially life-saving vaccine available completely free of charge, providing an important opportunity to protect children without placing a financial burden on families.

headline: Adviser calls for involving youth in policymaking
description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser on Education and Social Welfare Amir Abdullah has stressed that lasting peace...
author: APP
article_text:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser on Education and Social Welfare Amir Abdullah has stressed that lasting peace is essential for economic activity, business growth and social development, underscoring the vital role of young people in driving positive change in society.

“Young people are not only the leaders of tomorrow but also the leaders of today,” he said, emphasising the need to listen to their ideas, harness their potential and ensure their meaningful participation in policymaking.

He was addressing the inaugural session of a two-day youth engagement workshop for young people from the merged districts in Peshawar.

The workshop was organised by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Centre for Countering Violent Extremism in collaboration with the Sustainable Social Development Organisation and the British High Commission.

Abdullah said the initiative aimed to understand the challenges confronting young people in the merged districts, seek their recommendations and explore practical ways to promote peace and development.

He noted that young people had a better understanding of local needs and ground realities, making their involvement crucial to formulating effective policies and addressing issues related to peace and development.

Recalling his visits to the tribal districts during his tenure in the previous caretaker government, the adviser said his interactions with young people, tribal elders and government officials had provided valuable insights into the region’s challenges and priorities.

He observed that direct engagement with tribal youth had taught him more about the region than years of academic and professional involvement with tribal affairs.

The adviser said the workshop offered policymakers an important opportunity to learn from young people, understand their experiences and incorporate their perspectives into future decisions.

He expressed hope that the working groups formed during the two-day event would develop practical recommendations, adding that he would personally review their proposals for possible incorporation into future policymaking.

Other speakers on the opening day included Secretary Higher Education, Archives and Libraries Abidullah Kakakhel; former chairman of the Council of Islamic Ideology and Federal Shariat Court, Prof Qibla Ayaz; Director of the KP Centre for Countering Violent Extremism Dr Qasim Khan; Additional Director General Muhammad Kashif Irshad; and Sustainable Social Development Organisation Chief Executive Officer Syed Kausar Abbas.

headline: Auqaf dept orders crackdown on illegal land occupants
description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser on Auqaf Maulana Tayyab Qureshi has directed the department to launch a...
author: APP
article_text:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser on Auqaf Maulana Tayyab Qureshi has directed the department to launch a crackdown on illegal occupants of its properties and take practical steps to put vacant land to productive use and generate revenue.

He issued the directives while chairing a meeting on Auqaf properties here on Tuesday. Secretary Auqaf Muhammad Idrees, Auqaf Administrator Gul Nawaz Khan and other relevant officials attended the meeting.

The meeting reviewed the department’s properties, vacant plots, rental and lease income, outstanding dues, illegal occupants and the status of waqf land in Kalu Shah, Takht Bhai.

Officials briefed the meeting on encroachments involving private individuals and government departments, as well as efforts to recover outstanding dues.

Maulana Tayyab Qureshi directed the officials to prepare practical proposals for the effective utilisation of Auqaf land to enhance the department’s revenue.

He called for a comprehensive strategy to retrieve illegally occupied properties, stressing that the measures taken should deliver tangible results rather than remain limited to official paperwork.

Taking notice of outstanding dues owed by government departments, he directed the departments concerned to clear their payments without further delay.

He said Auqaf properties were a national trust and their protection, effective management and revenue generation must be accorded priority.

The adviser also directed officials to expedite the auction of waqf land in Kalu Shah, Takht Bhai, while ensuring compliance with all legal requirements and avoiding unnecessary delays.

He further ordered regular inspections of Auqaf properties and raids wherever necessary, warning that negligence in protecting departmental assets, removing encroachments and recovering outstanding dues would not be tolerated.

Emphasising the need for coordinated efforts to improve the department’s performance, he directed officials to resolve all pending matters within the stipulated timelines.

headline: Return of displaced persons from Tirah in phases announced
description: 24-member committee of tribal elders tasked with preparing a list of residents selected for the return.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
KHYBER: The Khyber district administration on Tuesday announced that a selected number of displaced persons from Tirah would be allowed to return in phases, with a 24-member committee of tribal elders tasked with preparing a list of those residents.

A notification issued by the Khyber House said that the administration, in consultation with the committee, would devise a plan for the organised and systematic return of around 600 displaced persons in phases.

It added that a list of selected persons would be issued by the district administration, with one person from each displaced family selected for return on a daily basis to prevent overcrowding and mismanagement during the process.

The notification said all selected persons would have to arrange their own transport for the journey to the valley. Only those whose names are approved by the administration will be allowed to leave for Tirah from the Naviya Kamar locality in Bara on the specified date.

“People whose names are not included in the initial lists shall wait for their turn and shall not come to Naviya Kamar in order to avoid any inconvenience,” it said.

Meanwhile, the Tehreek Mutasreen-i-Tirah (TMT) expressed reservations about the partial and limited return of internally displaced persons (IDPs), saying the new “mechanism” will add to their misery instead of alleviating their grievances.

Spokesman for the TMT Suhbat Khan Afridi told Dawn that it was unjust to the militancy-affected people of Tirah to allow only one person from each displaced family to return to the valley where there was a complete lack of basic necessities of life and the weather, too, was fast turning hostile.

He said one person from a family, without any government assistance, could neither repair the house nor rehabilitate the damaged structure in the valley.

Mr Afridi complained that the government was neither providing any financial assistance to these people nor giving them any food packages or non-food items, which were prerequisites for the return of an individual or a family.

He said mobility in the valley was also a problem because of excessive security checks and fears of militant attacks as the area had yet to be de-notified by the security forces.

“The government shall take our utter helplessness into consideration while devising a plan to send the displaced families back as most Tirah residents currently living in Bara and its suburbs are passing through a very difficult phase of their lives. Most of them have exhausted their financial resources and are unable to bear the cost of such a hasty return,” he said.

The spokesman urged authorities to arrange for the return of all displaced families from Tirah with honour and dignity while providing them with sufficient financial assistance to rebuild their homes and restart a decent life upon their return.

In September this year, the district administration had announced that all Tirah IDPs would return from Oct 10. However, the plan was later withdrawn without any reasons being cited, to the disappointment of thousands of Tirah residents.

KHYBER: The Khyber district administration on Tuesday announced that a selected number of displaced persons from Tirah would be allowed to return in phases, with a 24-member committee of tribal elders tasked with preparing a list of those residents.

A notification issued by the Khyber House said that the administration, in consultation with the committee, would devise a plan for the organised and systematic return of around 600 displaced persons in phases.

It added that a list of selected persons would be issued by the district administration, with one person from each displaced family selected for return on a daily basis to prevent overcrowding and mismanagement during the process.

The notification said all selected persons would have to arrange their own transport for the journey to the valley. Only those whose names are approved by the administration will be allowed to leave for Tirah from the Naviya Kamar locality in Bara on the specified date.

“People whose names are not included in the initial lists shall wait for their turn and shall not come to Naviya Kamar in order to avoid any inconvenience,” it said.

Meanwhile, the Tehreek Mutasreen-i-Tirah (TMT) expressed reservations about the partial and limited return of internally displaced persons (IDPs), saying the new “mechanism” will add to their misery instead of alleviating their grievances.

Spokesman for the TMT Suhbat Khan Afridi told Dawn that it was unjust to the militancy-affected people of Tirah to allow only one person from each displaced family to return to the valley where there was a complete lack of basic necessities of life and the weather, too, was fast turning hostile.

He said one person from a family, without any government assistance, could neither repair the house nor rehabilitate the damaged structure in the valley.

Mr Afridi complained that the government was neither providing any financial assistance to these people nor giving them any food packages or non-food items, which were prerequisites for the return of an individual or a family.

He said mobility in the valley was also a problem because of excessive security checks and fears of militant attacks as the area had yet to be de-notified by the security forces.

“The government shall take our utter helplessness into consideration while devising a plan to send the displaced families back as most Tirah residents currently living in Bara and its suburbs are passing through a very difficult phase of their lives. Most of them have exhausted their financial resources and are unable to bear the cost of such a hasty return,” he said.

The spokesman urged authorities to arrange for the return of all displaced families from Tirah with honour and dignity while providing them with sufficient financial assistance to rebuild their homes and restart a decent life upon their return.

In September this year, the district administration had announced that all Tirah IDPs would return from Oct 10. However, the plan was later withdrawn without any reasons being cited, to the disappointment of thousands of Tirah residents.

headline: AWKUM, Chinese varsity ink accord to boost research
description: MARDAN: Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan (AWKUM) and China’s Northwest A&F University (NWAFU), Yangling, on...
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
MARDAN: Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan (AWKUM) and China’s Northwest A&F University (NWAFU), Yangling, on Tuesday signed a cooperation agreement to strengthen joint research initiatives and academic training under the China Scholarship Council’s (CSC) “Special Programme for Talent Cultivation in Rural Revitalisation”.

The agreement was signed during a visit by a Chinese delegation to AWKUM and provides a framework for developing a joint implementation plan for research and academic training.

Under the agreement, AWKUM will host up to 11 students from NWAFU annually for three years, along with two visiting scholars each year, bringing the total number of visiting scholars to six over the agreement’s duration. Each scholar will be hosted for a period of up to 11 months to undertake academic and research activities in the field of rural revitalisation.

The participating students will be jointly supervised by faculty members from both universities, with a dedicated joint advisory committee established for each student. The China Scholarship Council will cover their airfare and living allowances.

The agreement will remain effective until Dec 31, 2029, providing a structured framework for sustained academic and research collaboration between the two institutions.

AWKUM Vice Chancellor Prof Jamil Ahmad, Director of the Office of Research, Innovation and Commercialisation (ORIC) Dr Tariq Mehmood, Prof Asad Ali, Dr Ziaul Islam and other university officials attended the signing ceremony.

Welcoming the visiting delegation, the university officials delivered a presentation highlighting AWKUM’s academic profile, research capabilities and expanding academic partnerships with Chinese institutions.

The Chinese delegation expressed keen interest in strengthening academic engagement with AWKUM and exploring further avenues of cooperation.

Both sides expressed confidence that the agreement would pave the way for new opportunities in research, academic exchange and institutional collaboration as Pakistan and China mark 75 years of diplomatic friendship.

At the conclusion of the visit, the guests were presented with commemorative shields and traditional Pakhtun shawls and caps as a gesture of goodwill and hospitality.

headline: Lawyers observe strike against suspension of PHC powers by FCC
description: Meeting decides to start indefinite strike if high court’s powers not restored by Nov 16.
author: Bureau Report
article_text:
PESHAWAR: The lawyers observed a strike across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Tuesday on the call of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Bar Council (KPBC) against the decision of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) regarding the suspension of the powers of the Peshawar High Court under Article 199 of the Constitution.

A meeting of lawyers organised by the Peshawar High Court Bar Association was also held, with participants threatening an indefinite strike in case the powers of the high court aren’t restored by Nov 16.

The lawyers mostly stayed away from the courts, including the Peshawar High Court at its principal seat in Peshawar and benches in other cities.

Meeting decides to start indefinite strike if high court’s powers not restored by 16th

The decision to boycott courts in the province was taken by the KPBC in an emergency general body meeting chaired by its vice-chairman, Mohammad Rafiq, on Nov 7.

The KPBC’s meeting, also attended by chairman of its executive committee Sardar Waqarul Mulk and other members, had voiced concern about the FCC decision regarding the suspension of the PHC’s powers whereby it was restrained from proceeding with petitions under Article 199 of the Constitution.

It maintained that the decision had usurped the basic rights in KP and that it was a great injustice to the people of the province.

The council said that it opposed undemocratic actions like the governor’s rule and emergency in the province and would raise its voice on every forum for restoration of democracy.

It also said that it had filed an application with the Federal Constitutional Court to become a party in the case related to cases registered under section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

The application has been filed through Bar Council member Babar Khan Yousafzai, in which along with becoming a party in the said cases, a request has been made to restore the constitutional jurisdiction of the Peshawar High Court in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 199 of the Constitution.

The council had passed a resolution in its general body meeting for filing the said application.

Meanwhile, a meeting of the representatives of different bar associations was held here on the premises of the PHC under the chairmanship of PHCBA president Aminur Rahman Yousafzai, which examined the situation emerging from the FCC’s order.

The meeting was attended by presidents of Peshawar High Court Bar Associations of Peshawar and its circuit benches at Bannu, Abbottabad and Dera Ismail Khan, general secretaries of Peshawar, Bannu and Abbottabad benches and presidents and general secretaries of bar associations of different districts.

Member of Pakistan Bar Council Naveed Akhtar and that of KPBC Babar Khan Yousafzai also attended the meeting. The participants expressed their views on the matter and made proposals.

The meeting unanimously decided that the struggle of lawyers’ bodies would continue until the restoration of the high court powers under Article 199 of the Constitution.

It demanded that the matter pending with the FCC be taken up for hearing today (Wednesday).

The meeting decided that PHCBA President Aminur Rahman would contact all stakeholders to ask them to play their role in restoring the PHC powers until Nov 16.

It also decided that the PHC bar associations would become party to the matter pending before the FCC.

It also made a decision to convene an All Pakistan Lawyers Convention under the supervision of all the bar councils in the country.

Last Thursday, a two-member FCC bench declared: “Since the armed forces have been called to act in aid of civil power in the entire province of KP pursuant to the Oct 11 order, the proceedings before PHC instituted under Article 199 on or after Oct 12 shall, in terms of Clause 4 of Article 245, remain suspended.”

Following the FCC order, the PHC’s administrative committee on Friday decided not to proceed with petitions filed under Article 199 on or after Oct 12. It also decided not to entertain fresh petitions and return them to petitioners, directing them to approach the “appropriate” forum.

The decision has affected several high-profile cases filed under Article 199, including petitions against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. It also hit petitions regarding the alleged illegal detention or “abduction” of non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and several other PTI lawmakers and leaders.

A meeting of lawyers organised by the Peshawar High Court Bar Association was also held, with participants threatening an indefinite strike in case the powers of the high court aren’t restored by Nov 16.

The lawyers mostly stayed away from the courts, including the Peshawar High Court at its principal seat in Peshawar and benches in other cities.

Meeting decides to start indefinite strike if high court’s powers not restored by 16th

The decision to boycott courts in the province was taken by the KPBC in an emergency general body meeting chaired by its vice-chairman, Mohammad Rafiq, on Nov 7.

The KPBC’s meeting, also attended by chairman of its executive committee Sardar Waqarul Mulk and other members, had voiced concern about the FCC decision regarding the suspension of the PHC’s powers whereby it was restrained from proceeding with petitions under Article 199 of the Constitution.

It maintained that the decision had usurped the basic rights in KP and that it was a great injustice to the people of the province.

The council said that it opposed undemocratic actions like the governor’s rule and emergency in the province and would raise its voice on every forum for restoration of democracy.

It also said that it had filed an application with the Federal Constitutional Court to become a party in the case related to cases registered under section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

The application has been filed through Bar Council member Babar Khan Yousafzai, in which along with becoming a party in the said cases, a request has been made to restore the constitutional jurisdiction of the Peshawar High Court in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 199 of the Constitution.

The council had passed a resolution in its general body meeting for filing the said application.

Meanwhile, a meeting of the representatives of different bar associations was held here on the premises of the PHC under the chairmanship of PHCBA president Aminur Rahman Yousafzai, which examined the situation emerging from the FCC’s order.

The meeting was attended by presidents of Peshawar High Court Bar Associations of Peshawar and its circuit benches at Bannu, Abbottabad and Dera Ismail Khan, general secretaries of Peshawar, Bannu and Abbottabad benches and presidents and general secretaries of bar associations of different districts.

Member of Pakistan Bar Council Naveed Akhtar and that of KPBC Babar Khan Yousafzai also attended the meeting. The participants expressed their views on the matter and made proposals.

The meeting unanimously decided that the struggle of lawyers’ bodies would continue until the restoration of the high court powers under Article 199 of the Constitution.

It demanded that the matter pending with the FCC be taken up for hearing today (Wednesday).

The meeting decided that PHCBA President Aminur Rahman would contact all stakeholders to ask them to play their role in restoring the PHC powers until Nov 16.

It also decided that the PHC bar associations would become party to the matter pending before the FCC.

It also made a decision to convene an All Pakistan Lawyers Convention under the supervision of all the bar councils in the country.

The decision has affected several high-profile cases filed under Article 199, including petitions against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. It also hit petitions regarding the alleged illegal detention or “abduction” of non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and several other PTI lawmakers and leaders.

headline: Matric exams postponed in North Waziristan
description: BANNU: The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE), Bannu, has postponed the Secondary School...
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
BANNU: The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE), Bannu, has postponed the Secondary School Certificate Second Annual Examination in North Waziristan due to the security situation while a curfew has also been imposed in the district’s Mir Ali area.

The postponement of the exams was announced in a press release by the BISE on Nov 9, following the North Waziristan deputy commissioner’s instructions.

A revised schedule for the examinations would be announced later, the press release said, adding that examinations at centres set up at Cadet College Razmak and in Bakakhel tehsil would be held as per schedule.

In North Waziristan, this is the second time that these exams — scheduled to start on Oct 12 — have been postponed. They were initiallypostponedlast month, not just in North Waziristan but also in Bannu and Lakki Marwat.

Meanwhile, a curfew was imposed in areas from Bobali and Mir Ali up to Isha, an official statement by the district administration said. The curfew would remain in place until the completion of an ongoing security operation in these areas.

The Bannu-Miramshah Road will also remain closed for traffic during this period.

Area Representative and Development Council member Malik Rohullah Khan said the general officer commanding north had issued instructions for the curfew.

However, he added, residents had been allowed to visit markets for the purchase of essential daily-use items in Miramshah and Datta Khel on his request.

He further stated that residents wishing to travel outside North Waziristan could use the Miramshah, Isha and Razmak routes.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including North Waziristan, has been facing security challenges for a long time.

Security forcesconductedan intelligence-based operation in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali on Monday and neutralised two terrorist hideouts, the military’s media wing said the previous day.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, security forces recovered a huge cache of prepared improvised explosive devices, explosive preparation material, weapons, and ammunition from hideouts, which were established inside mosques.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: One dead, five injured in Kohistan road accident
description: MANSEHRA: A man was killed, and five members of his family were injured when two excavators being transported on a...
author: A Correspondent
article_text:
MANSEHRA: A man was killed, and five members of his family were injured when two excavators being transported on a trailer fell onto their pick-up vehicle in the Changal area of Lower Kohistan district on Tuesday.

“Police personnel retrieved the injured from the wreckage of the vehicle and rushed them to a nearby health facility,” Lower Kohistan District Police Officer (DPO) Zafar Ahmad Khan told reporters.

He said the excavators were being transported via the Karakoram Highway when the trailer driver took a sharp turn, causing the machines to fall onto a pick-up truck.

Six members of a family travelling in the pick-up sustained critical injuries and were shifted to a nearby health facility, where doctors pronounced one of them dead.

The deceased was identified as Ahsan Qayyum, while the injured, including Shah Faisal, Bushra Bibi, Arif Khan, Mohammad Arif and Nasser Khan, were referred to Ayub Medical Complex Hospital in Abbottabad. They belonged to Kolai-Palas district.

Meanwhile, police have arrested two suspects for allegedly assaulting a woman after forcibly entering her house and making explicit videos and photographs of the victim to blackmail her in the Jabori area of Siren Valley.

The victim, while lodging an FIR with Shinkiari police last week, alleged that Abdul Malik and his accomplice, Siddique Latif, barged into her house and assaulted her.

headline: Four killed as car ambushed in Swabi
description: SWABI: Four people, including two passersby, were killed and nine others injured when a car was ambushed in the...
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
SWABI: Four people, including two passersby, were killed and nine others injured when a car was ambushed in the limits of Zaida police station here on Tuesday.

Police said that Manzoor Khan, a resident of Marghuz village, was travelling in his car, along with his two gunmen, on Swabi-Jehangira Road when he came under attack near the district headquarters.

The police said that Manzoor sustained injuries in the attack, while his two gunmen, identified as Mohammad Ghaffar and Sabirullah, died on the spot.

Two other persons, including a woman, the wife of Hamid Khan, and a cleric, Maulana Aftab, who were passing by the area at the time of firing, were also killed.

Zaida police station SHO Raz Mohammad said the car attack was the result of an old enmity. He said police had arrested two suspects in connection with the killings.

He said the rest of the injured were also passersby. They were identified as Rehman Sher, Zahid Gilani, Imran Khan, Aamir Khan, Yousuf Khan, Mohammad Atiq and Masood Khan. The identity of an injured person could not be ascertained. They were taken to different hospitals for treatment.

Meanwhile, the deaths of the woman and the cleric, who was the prayer leader of a mosque in the Torkhel area of Swabi city, sparked a protest at Karnal Sher Chowk.

The protesters demanded the arrest of those involved in the killings of the two passersby.

In another incident, a seven-year-old boy, Mohammad Azlan, a student of a private school, was killed while getting off his school bus on Tuesday, according to his family and police.

They said the child reportedly fell under the wheel of the bus while alighting and died on the spot.
