headline: Hidden cause of economic imbalances
description: A relatively small segment commands a disproportionately large share of purchasing power and assets.
author: Shahid Kardar
article_text:
GROWING inequality is a serious economic and social issue. Internally, we tend to treat poverty and inequality as separate problems. They are closely connected but not identical. Poverty is about deprivation; inequality is about how income, wealth, opportunities, and economic power are dis­­tributed. An economy can grow and even red­u­­ce poverty temporarily while allowing wealth and privilege to become concentrated.

Household data underlines the problem. The consumption-based Gini coefficient increased from 28.4 in 2018 –19 to 32.7 in 2024 –25. This figure does not capture the full extent of inequality in income and wealth, be­­cause household surveys tend to underrepresent the assets and incomes of the richest households.

The distribution of income and wealth influences what people consume, what businesses produce, where investment flows, and how much a country imports. In Pakistan, a relatively small segment commands a disproportionately large share of purchasing power and assets, while much of the population struggles to meet basic needs.

A relatively small segment commands a disproportionately large share of purchasing power and assets.

The benefits of economic growth have been distributed unevenly. Expanding sectors such as banking, telecommunications, IT, energy, oil and gas require capital, technology, and specialised skills, favouring those who already possess financial resources or access to quality education. The state’s failure to provide decent education and healthcare has denied much of the population a fair opportunity to participate in these activities. Hence, economic disadvantages are passed from one generation to the next.

Equally damaging is the continued protection of selected businesses from competition through high import duties, subsidies, tax exemptions, and special regulatory concessions. Powerful business groups have resisted competition, sometimes forming cartels to influence prices and markets. Profits earned through state protection rather than efficiency reward influence instead of innovation, raise costs for consumers, and weaken competitiveness.

The tax system has reinforced these inequalities by treating similar incomes from different sources unequally. Salaried individuals face substantial income taxes, while earnings from property, capital gains, and certain commercial activities have historically enjoyed relatively favourable treatment.

The state itself has been a major contributor to wealth concentration. Valuable public land and plots have been given to officials and influential individuals, while discretionary powers over building permissions, zoning regulations, and public contracts have created opportunities for private enrichment. Rising property prices, reinforced by speculative investment and the use of real estate to park undeclared wealth, have further increased the fortunes of existing asset owners. Corruption, smuggling, tax evasion, and manipulation of import and export prices have provided additional avenues for accumulating wealth, often beyond the reach of effective taxation and accountability.

Together, these factors constitute a system in which public authority is used to transfer economic opportunities and resources to privileged groups. The consequences extend beyond unfair income distribution; they also distort how the economy allocates and uses its scarce resources.

When fortunes can be made through political connections, regulatory concessions, and protection from competition, capital and entrepreneurial talent are diverted towards securing favours rather than productive investment. It becomes more profitable to lobby for higher import duties or special exemptions than to invest in technology, improve quality, or develop export markets.

The concentration of purchasing power also shapes the structure of domestic demand and, therefore, what businesses choose to produce. Businesses often respond to this purchasing power by directing investment towards activities serving a narrow market.

Meanwhile, the limited purchasing power of the majority constrains demand for mass-consumption goods, discouraging investment in industries that could serve a broader domestic market, create jobs, and compete globally.

This distorted pattern of consumption and production also contributes to our recurring external imbalances. The concentration of disposable income generates demand for imported vehicles, electronics, luxury goods, foreign travel, and education abroad, adding to the foreign exchange needed for machinery, fuel, technology, and industrial inputs. Not all imports are undesirable. Many are essential for productivity and exports. However, our consumption and production structures generate substantial demand for foreign exchange without a corresponding capacity to earn it through competitive exports.

Remittances from overseas Pakistanis have helped bridge this gap. But however valuable these inflows, they cannot substitute indefinitely for an economy capable of financing its import requirements through its own export earnings.

Inequality is certainly not the sole cause of external deficits. Exchange rate policies, tariffs, energy costs, inflation, low productivity, and weak export competitiveness also matter. Still, the concentration of purchasing power helps explain why import demand remains substantial even when we face severe foreign exchange constraints. There is another damaging effect.

When influential groups secure tax exemptions, subsidies, and protected markets, government revenues suffer. The burden of financing an oversized, extractive state, with its extensive controls and perks and privileges, consequently falls disproportionately on salaried workers, compliant businesses, and ordinary consumers unable to escape taxation.

Public expenditure compounds the problem. Chronic underinvestment in quality education and healthcare has denied millions of children a fair start. Affluent households can purchase good private education and medical care, while poorer families depend on poor and overstretched public services. Their children’s prospects depend on family circumstances. The failure to provide equal opportunities thereby perpetuates inequality across generations.

Addressing these disparities does not mean pe­­nalising wealth creation. It means distinguishing wealth earned through enterprise, innovation, and productivity from fortunes accumulated through political connections, monopolies, and state-gra­nted privileges. This requires a fairer tax system.

Protection must give way to competition, while discretionary allocations of public land, contracts, and regulatory concessions need to be replaced by transparent, rule-based processes. Foreign aid, remittances, and favourable global developments have provided only temporary relief, enabling successive governments to shelve tough reforms, thereby sustaining an economic structure that rewards privilege over productivity.

Unless this system of privileges and unequal opportunities is dismantled, Pakistan will remain trapped in recurring internal and external imbalances, regardless of how many stabilisation programmes it negotiates with the IMF and others.

The writer is a former governor of the State Bank.

This distorted pattern of consumption and production also contributes to our recurring external imbalances. The concentration of disposable income generates demand for imported vehicles, electronics, luxury goods, foreign travel, and education abroad, adding to the foreign exchange needed for machinery, fuel, technology, and industrial inputs. Not all imports are undesirable. Many are essential for productivity and exports. However, our consumption and production structures generate substantial demand for foreign exchange without a corresponding capacity to earn it through competitive exports.

Remittances from overseas Pakistanis have helped bridge this gap. But however valuable these inflows, they cannot substitute indefinitely for an economy capable of financing its import requirements through its own export earnings.

Inequality is certainly not the sole cause of external deficits. Exchange rate policies, tariffs, energy costs, inflation, low productivity, and weak export competitiveness also matter. Still, the concentration of purchasing power helps explain why import demand remains substantial even when we face severe foreign exchange constraints. There is another damaging effect.

When influential groups secure tax exemptions, subsidies, and protected markets, government revenues suffer. The burden of financing an oversized, extractive state, with its extensive controls and perks and privileges, consequently falls disproportionately on salaried workers, compliant businesses, and ordinary consumers unable to escape taxation.

Public expenditure compounds the problem. Chronic underinvestment in quality education and healthcare has denied millions of children a fair start. Affluent households can purchase good private education and medical care, while poorer families depend on poor and overstretched public services. Their children’s prospects depend on family circumstances. The failure to provide equal opportunities thereby perpetuates inequality across generations.

Addressing these disparities does not mean pe­­nalising wealth creation. It means distinguishing wealth earned through enterprise, innovation, and productivity from fortunes accumulated through political connections, monopolies, and state-gra­nted privileges. This requires a fairer tax system.

Protection must give way to competition, while discretionary allocations of public land, contracts, and regulatory concessions need to be replaced by transparent, rule-based processes. Foreign aid, remittances, and favourable global developments have provided only temporary relief, enabling successive governments to shelve tough reforms, thereby sustaining an economic structure that rewards privilege over productivity.

Unless this system of privileges and unequal opportunities is dismantled, Pakistan will remain trapped in recurring internal and external imbalances, regardless of how many stabilisation programmes it negotiates with the IMF and others.

The writer is a former governor of the State Bank.

headline: US court rules SpaceX must face sex-bias claims
description: US appeals court rejects company's request to send the case to private arbitration.
author: Reuters
article_text:
San Francisco: SpaceX must face a lawsuit accusing it of illegally firing eight engineers who raised concerns about alleged sexual harassment and discrimination at the company after a US appeals court on Tuesday rejected its request to send the case to private arbitration.

The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a federal judge’s ruling that the engineers’ claims were exempt from the arbitration agreements they signed at SpaceX and can continue in court.

Spokespeople for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the decision.

The engineers’ attorney, Laurie Burgess, said they were “delighted” with the court’s “well-reasoned” decision.

The engineers filed the lawsuit in 2024, claiming SpaceX CEO Elon Musk ordered their firing after they circulated a letter calling the billionaire a “distraction and embarrassment” and urging executives to disavow sexually charged comments he made on social media.

The lawsuit said Musk’s conduct fostered a “pervasively sexist culture” at SpaceX where female engineers were routinely subjected to harassment and sexist comments. SpaceX has denied the allegations.

The 9th Circuit on Tuesday rejected SpaceX’s argument that the claims were not covered by a federal law that allows individuals to pursue lawsuits in “sexual harassment disputes” regardless of arbitration agreements.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Pakistan pushing for diplomacy amid global tensions
description: University of Chicago scholar urges Pakistan to capitalise on ties with both US and China, shore up its "middle power" status.
author: Kalbe Ali
article_text:
• Strength at home and effective diplomacy abroad key to confronting emerging world order, Dar tells Margalla Dialogue • University of Chicago scholar says US can’t win Iran war; claims Washington complicit in Palestinian ‘genocide’ by Israel • Urges Pakistan to capitalise on ties with both US and China, shore up its ‘middle power’ status

ISLAMABAD: Calling for stronger diplomacy, dialogue and multilateral cooperation to address growing global tensions, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar here on Tuesday stressed that Pakistan would continue to work for regional peace, while safeguarding its sovereignty and national interests.

Addressing the Margalla Dialogue 2026, organised by the Islamabad Policy Research Institute (IPRI), he highlighted that the shape of the emerging world order remains uncertain. “The choices countries make during this transition will help determine whether it produces greater cooperation or deeper confrontation,” he said.

“The international security architecture faces mounting pressure. Intensifying great power rivalries, protracted conflicts and erosion of arms control agreements are increasing the risks of confrontation and miscalculation,” he noted, addressing the theme of this year’s dialogue, ‘Global Order in Transition: Navigating Strategic Uncertainty’.

Posing the question “how can we safeguard our security and build a more prosperous future for our people?”, Mr Dar maintained that the answer lies in “strength at home and effective diplomacy abroad”.

He noted that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, was a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective security and credible deterrence, rather than targeting any particular country.

Discussing Pakistan’s international partnerships, he described relations with China as a cornerstone of the country’s foreign policy, while highlighting constructive engagement with the United States and expanding cooperation with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, Iran, Gulf countries, Europe and Central Asia.

He reiterated that Pakistan sought peace but would firmly defend its sovereignty, stressing that a just settlement of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with UN Secu­rity Council resolutions was essential for lasting peace in the region.

He also warned against Indian attempts to weaponise water, adding that Pakistan would safeguard its rights under the Indus Waters Treaty.

Mr Dar also classified terrorism emanating from Afghan territory as a serious security challenge, adding that Pakistan would continue protecting its people while supporting a peaceful, stable and economically integrated Afghanistan.

With regard to the Middle East, the foreign minister said Pakistan’s facilitation of the Islamabad talks between the United States and Iran in April had reflected its commitment to resolving conflicts through dialogue.

Other panel discussions at the event also featured noted national and international speakers. In his keynote address during a discussion on ‘Geopolitics and the Realignment of Global Power’, Prof John J. Mearsheimer, from the University of Chicago, spoke at length about the losses incurred by the US and Israel in the war against Iran, as well as the policy failures of the Trump administration.

“Trump just dismissed the views of his principal advisers and he decided instead he would listen to Netanyahu and the head of Mos­sad,” he said, adding that the two men convinced the US president that attacking Iran was a good idea.

“The decision to get into this war was an irrational decision… The US is in a war that it is going to lose, there is no way the US can defeat Iran,” he said.

He categorically said that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza as a means to driving Palestinians from their own territory. “That is why they are treating the Palest­in­i­ans in Gaza today in the most horrendous ways… and launching pogroms against Palestinians in the (occupied) West Bank,” he said, adding that despite their brutal methods, they had failed to achieve their objective of driving the Palestinians out.

He was quite clear that Israel could not have committed this genocide without US assistance, adding that Washington was complicit in this crime, providing diplomatic support to Israel and vetoing six UN Security Council resolutions designed to shut down the genocide.

Talking about the contours of great power politics, he said that the world has shifted from a unipolar world into a multipolar world. “There are now three great powers in the world: the US, China and Russia,” he said, adding that the dynamics of a unipolar world were very different from the dynamics of a multipolar world.

Noting that nothing is going to change in the relationship between Pakistan and India, Prof Mearsheimer said that India could not become a great power in the near future, as it is plagued by too many issues, though it could become a formidable middle power, like Japan. Pakistan, he said, needed to strive for wealth creation to become a middle power like Germany and Japan.

Pakistan, he said, was in an ideal position in the multipolar world, as it has cordial ties with both the US and China, and hasn’t had to choose between the two.

As long as the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East persist, the US will continue to pivot away from East Asia, he said, noting how nice Trump is to Xi Jinping because he doesn’t want to antagonise Beijing.

Noted Middle East scholar Dr Vali Nasr lauded the resilience and tactics of Iran that had led to a failure of US and Israeli policies.

However, he maintained that Israel had an expansionist agenda and the war between Israel and Iran was still unfinished, adding that a military alliance between India, UAE and Israel could pose a threat to Pakistan.

He added that US involvement in Iran and Ukraine had led to softening its military presence against China in the Far East, and soon all­ies like Japan and South Korea too will start reconsidering their age-old reliance on the US for security.

The actions and statements of President Trump have prompted demands from Iran to quit the Nuclear Non Proliferation Treaty, he said. Former US diplomat Robin Raphel noted that if Iran leaves the NPT, it could trigger exits by other countries too.

Former senator Mushahid Hussain Syed said that there was a time when decisions were made in Washington regarding other countries. “But now regime change in US is due to Iran,” he mused, recalling the recent midterm elections.

• Strength at home and effective diplomacy abroad key to confronting emerging world order, Dar tells Margalla Dialogue
• University of Chicago scholar says US can’t win Iran war; claims Washington complicit in Palestinian ‘genocide’ by Israel
• Urges Pakistan to capitalise on ties with both US and China, shore up its ‘middle power’ status

ISLAMABAD: Calling for stronger diplomacy, dialogue and multilateral cooperation to address growing global tensions, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar here on Tuesday stressed that Pakistan would continue to work for regional peace, while safeguarding its sovereignty and national interests.

Addressing the Margalla Dialogue 2026, organised by the Islamabad Policy Research Institute (IPRI), he highlighted that the shape of the emerging world order remains uncertain. “The choices countries make during this transition will help determine whether it produces greater cooperation or deeper confrontation,” he said.

“The international security architecture faces mounting pressure. Intensifying great power rivalries, protracted conflicts and erosion of arms control agreements are increasing the risks of confrontation and miscalculation,” he noted, addressing the theme of this year’s dialogue, ‘Global Order in Transition: Navigating Strategic Uncertainty’.

Posing the question “how can we safeguard our security and build a more prosperous future for our people?”, Mr Dar maintained that the answer lies in “strength at home and effective diplomacy abroad”.

He noted that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, was a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective security and credible deterrence, rather than targeting any particular country.

Discussing Pakistan’s international partnerships, he described relations with China as a cornerstone of the country’s foreign policy, while highlighting constructive engagement with the United States and expanding cooperation with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, Iran, Gulf countries, Europe and Central Asia.

He reiterated that Pakistan sought peace but would firmly defend its sovereignty, stressing that a just settlement of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with UN Secu­rity Council resolutions was essential for lasting peace in the region.

He also warned against Indian attempts to weaponise water, adding that Pakistan would safeguard its rights under the Indus Waters Treaty.

Mr Dar also classified terrorism emanating from Afghan territory as a serious security challenge, adding that Pakistan would continue protecting its people while supporting a peaceful, stable and economically integrated Afghanistan.

With regard to the Middle East, the foreign minister said Pakistan’s facilitation of the Islamabad talks between the United States and Iran in April had reflected its commitment to resolving conflicts through dialogue.

Other panel discussions at the event also featured noted national and international speakers. In his keynote address during a discussion on ‘Geopolitics and the Realignment of Global Power’, Prof John J. Mearsheimer, from the University of Chicago, spoke at length about the losses incurred by the US and Israel in the war against Iran, as well as the policy failures of the Trump administration.

“Trump just dismissed the views of his principal advisers and he decided instead he would listen to Netanyahu and the head of Mos­sad,” he said, adding that the two men convinced the US president that attacking Iran was a good idea.

“The decision to get into this war was an irrational decision… The US is in a war that it is going to lose, there is no way the US can defeat Iran,” he said.

He categorically said that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza as a means to driving Palestinians from their own territory. “That is why they are treating the Palest­in­i­ans in Gaza today in the most horrendous ways… and launching pogroms against Palestinians in the (occupied) West Bank,” he said, adding that despite their brutal methods, they had failed to achieve their objective of driving the Palestinians out.

He was quite clear that Israel could not have committed this genocide without US assistance, adding that Washington was complicit in this crime, providing diplomatic support to Israel and vetoing six UN Security Council resolutions designed to shut down the genocide.

Talking about the contours of great power politics, he said that the world has shifted from a unipolar world into a multipolar world. “There are now three great powers in the world: the US, China and Russia,” he said, adding that the dynamics of a unipolar world were very different from the dynamics of a multipolar world.

Noting that nothing is going to change in the relationship between Pakistan and India, Prof Mearsheimer said that India could not become a great power in the near future, as it is plagued by too many issues, though it could become a formidable middle power, like Japan. Pakistan, he said, needed to strive for wealth creation to become a middle power like Germany and Japan.

Pakistan, he said, was in an ideal position in the multipolar world, as it has cordial ties with both the US and China, and hasn’t had to choose between the two.

As long as the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East persist, the US will continue to pivot away from East Asia, he said, noting how nice Trump is to Xi Jinping because he doesn’t want to antagonise Beijing.

Noted Middle East scholar Dr Vali Nasr lauded the resilience and tactics of Iran that had led to a failure of US and Israeli policies.

However, he maintained that Israel had an expansionist agenda and the war between Israel and Iran was still unfinished, adding that a military alliance between India, UAE and Israel could pose a threat to Pakistan.

He added that US involvement in Iran and Ukraine had led to softening its military presence against China in the Far East, and soon all­ies like Japan and South Korea too will start reconsidering their age-old reliance on the US for security.

The actions and statements of President Trump have prompted demands from Iran to quit the Nuclear Non Proliferation Treaty, he said. Former US diplomat Robin Raphel noted that if Iran leaves the NPT, it could trigger exits by other countries too.

Former senator Mushahid Hussain Syed said that there was a time when decisions were made in Washington regarding other countries. “But now regime change in US is due to Iran,” he mused, recalling the recent midterm elections.

headline: Remittances increase 14pc to $14.8bn in four months
description: Workers’ remittances increase by 13.8pc year-on-year in October, taking cumulative growth to 14pc in the first four months of FY27.
author: Shahid Iqbal
article_text:
KARACHI: Workers’ remittances increased by 13.8 per cent year-on-year in October, taking cumulative growth to 14pc in the first four months of FY27 and putting inflows on track to meet the State Bank’s annual target of $45 billion.

According to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data released on Tuesday, the country received $3.9 billion from overseas Pakistanis in October, up 13.8pc from a year ago and 8.5pc from September.

Cumulatively, inflows rose to $14.8bn during July-October FY27, compared with $13bn in the corresponding period last year.

SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad recently set the remittance target at $45bn for FY27 after sustained inflows exceeded $41bn in FY26, making inflows from overseas Pakistanis the most important source of foreign exchange.

The continued growth is particularly significant given concerns that the prolonged conflict in the Gulf region could disrupt employment and earnings of millions of Pakistani workers. Despite the regional tensions, remittance inflows have remained resilient.

The increase also reflects the growing number of Pakistanis seeking employment abroad. Millions of workers, including highly skilled professionals, have left the country over the past three years. The government has also pursued a policy of exporting manpower to generate foreign exchange, although the departure of skilled workers has raised concerns about the domestic workforce.

Saudi Arabia remained the largest source of remittances during July-October FY27, with inflows reaching $3.668bn, an increase of 16.5pc against 7.7pc in the same period last year.

The United Kingdom recorded the highest growth among major remittance destinations. Inflows rose 19.2pc to $2.226bn, compared with a 5.4pc rise the previous year.

Remittances from the United Arab Emirates (UAE), despite exposure to regional conflict, increased by 13.5pc to $3.051bn in 4MFY27. However, the growth rate was lower than the 15.2pc recorded in the corresponding period last year.

Other significant sources included European Union countries, which contributed $1.866bn, followed by the US at $1.259bn and other Gulf Cooperation Council countries at $1.374bn during the July-October period of 2026-27.

In October alone, Saudi Arabia remained the largest contributor, sending $981.6 million. The UAE followed with $815.9m, while inflows from the UK stood at $592.2m, EU countries at $461m and the US at $328.9m.

headline: Delays fail to dampen interest in Islamabad LG polls as over 3,500 file nominations
description: 3,505 candidates who have filed the nominations include 110 women.
author: Kashif Abbasi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: Repeated postponements of the local government elections in Islamabad in the last around six years have failed to dampen public interest in the system as over 3,500 candidates have filed nomination papers for the December 20 polls.

The 3,505 candidates who filed the nominations included 110 women, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) was informed on Tuesday.

The scrutiny of the papers will begin on Wednesday, officials told a special meeting of the ECP held at the Election Commission Secretariat to review the arrangements for the polls.

The meeting was chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja and attended by members of the commission, Interior Secretary Ahmed Raza Sarwar and other senior officers.

The commission was briefed on the Islamabad local government system, the procedure for elections to various seats and the steps taken so far by the ECP. The process to procure the election materials and arrangements for printing of the ballot papers have been completed.

The meeting was told that the commission was in contact with all relevant institutions and ready to hold the elections. The interior secretary assured the ECP that the Ministry of Interior would extend all possible cooperation for the peaceful conduct of the local government elections.

The chief commissioner Islamabad said instructions had been issued to all returning officers to perform their duties in accordance with the Constitution and law and the ECP’s election programme. He said work was underway on the preparation of the list of polling stations, transportation and security plans.

He said as soon as the list of polling stations was published and the transportation and security plans were completed, copies would be provided to the ECP. Foolproof arrangements would be ensured for holding the local body elections.

The district returning officer told the meeting that he was personally supervising all stages of the election and the transportation plan was being finalised to facilitate and provide security to the polling staff.

The SSP operations said that 15,000 personnel would be deployed to maintain law and order, while additional force required would be requisitioned from Punjab.

The commission asked the Islamabad administration to submit the security and transport plans. The chief election commissioner directed that effective security arrangements be ensured during the elections.

He also directed the district monitoring officer to strictly enforce the code of conduct, making it clear that no negligence would be tolerated.

It is relevant to note here that Pattan-Coalition38 (a network of associations, community-based organisations, labour unions and human rights activists) in its research report released in February this year soon after postponement of elections had stated: “Repeated postponement of the local government elections in Islamabad [five times in five years] represents a direct assault on grassroots democracy and raises serious concerns about the subordination of the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) to the executive.”

The report stated that democratic participation in the federal capital had been systematically obstructed, at enormous financial and political cost.

The research report had pointed out that a total of 7,866 candidates in two aborted elections collectively paid Rs37.74 million in nomination fees. Beyond this, candidates spent heavily on legal representation and campaign mobilisation. The total estimated expenditure for the two cancelled elections stood at Rs544.30 million.

“This is not merely financial loss; it is the erosion of citizens’ constitutional right to representation too,” added the report. It stated that more than one-third of respondents [in the survey] believed that the elections were postponed out of the fear of defeat by the ruling parties. It stated that nearly 40pc of the respondents blamed the bureaucracy, alleging their resistance to working under elected representatives.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Student injured as roof of Faisalabad classroom caves in
description: Private school sealed; action ordered against administration.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
TOBA TEK SINGH: A ninth grade student was seriously wounded when the dilapidated roof of a classroom of a private school collapsed at Chak 132-RB, Sahuwala, of Chak Jhumra tehsil on Tuesday.

As per the school administration, no other student was present in the classroom when its roof caved in at Alflah Grammar School.

The injured student, identified as Sajjad Zahid (14), was shifted to Chak Jhumra THQ Hospital.

On the direction of the Faisalabad District Education Authority CEO, the school’s building has been sealed and further legal action against its administration has been ordered for running the institute in a rundown building.

Private school sealed; action ordered against administration

SUSPECT HELD: Mian Channu police arrested on Tuesday a juvenile suspect who allegedly strangled a minor boy to death for resisting rape attempt at Chak 75/15-L.

Police sources say that the suspect, Adeel (15) allegedly lured eight-year-old Zain to fields outside the village where he attempted to rape him.

As Zain raised an alarm and offered resistance, the suspect allegedly strangled him to death and fled the scene.

On being informed of the incident, a police team reached the village and started investigations.

As per sources, the police traced the suspect through geofencing and arrested him within a few hours.

SUSPECT KILLED: An alleged robber was killed in an “encounter” with Shorkot Cantonment Crime Control Department (CCD) team late on Monday night.

According to a CCD official, a team was patrolling near Chak 500-JB, Padrianwala, when it confronted two men riding a motorcycle. On seeing the police, the official says, the two suspects opened indiscriminate fire, leaving Constable Babar injured. He was shifted to the Shorkot THQ Hospital.

The official says the policemen returned the fire.Following the crossfire, the police found one of the suspects lying dead, while the other fled away.

He says the dead suspect was identified as Bilal (24) of Basti Hussainabad, who was wanted by police in several robbery cases.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

Private school sealed; action ordered against administration

SUSPECT HELD: Mian Channu police arrested on Tuesday a juvenile suspect who allegedly strangled a minor boy to death for resisting rape attempt at Chak 75/15-L.

Police sources say that the suspect, Adeel (15) allegedly lured eight-year-old Zain to fields outside the village where he attempted to rape him.

As Zain raised an alarm and offered resistance, the suspect allegedly strangled him to death and fled the scene.

On being informed of the incident, a police team reached the village and started investigations.

As per sources, the police traced the suspect through geofencing and arrested him within a few hours.

According to a CCD official, a team was patrolling near Chak 500-JB, Padrianwala, when it confronted two men riding a motorcycle. On seeing the police, the official says, the two suspects opened indiscriminate fire, leaving Constable Babar injured. He was shifted to the Shorkot THQ Hospital.

The official says the policemen returned the fire.Following the crossfire, the police found one of the suspects lying dead, while the other fled away.

He says the dead suspect was identified as Bilal (24) of Basti Hussainabad, who was wanted by police in several robbery cases.

headline: Islamabad ATC refuses to drop terror charges in PAF officer murder case
description: Prosecutor argues it is premature to question the applicability of the charges as no prosecution witness has yet been examined.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Tuesday rejected a defence plea seeking the removal of terrorism-related charges from the murder case of late Group Captain Asim Tariq, ruling that the trial would continue before the anti-terrorism court.

ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Mohammad Zulqarnain announced the decision after hearing arguments from the defence counsel and prosecutor.

During the proceedings, the defence counsel argued that the provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act were not applicable to the case and requested the court to decide the matter before recording statements of prosecution witnesses.

However, the prosecutor opposed the plea, arguing that the nature and circumstances of the incident warranted the inclusion of terrorism charges. He maintained that the court could proceed with recording prosecution witnesses’ statements in light of precedents set by higher courts.

The prosecutor further argued that if the court found at any stage of the trial that the terrorism provisions were not applicable, it had the authority to transfer the case to the appropriate forum. He said it was premature to question the applicability of the charges as no prosecution witness had yet been examined.

The judge initially reserved the decision on the defence application and took a brief recess. After resuming the proceedings, he dismissed the plea and directed that the trial proceed before the ATC.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Iran’s Pezeshkian to raise US, Israeli ‘environmental crimes’ at COP31
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said he will use the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkiye to highlight what he...
article_text:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said he will use the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkiye to highlight what he described as US and Israeli crimes against Iran’s environment, Al Jazeera reports.

“The UN climate summit is a good opportunity to discuss the actions the US and Israel have taken to damage the environment in Iran and the region,” Pezeshkian says before departing for Antalya, according to Iran’s Fars news agency.

He also says he would raise Tehran’s position during bilateral meetings with other world leaders. “We will discuss the legitimate positions of the Islamic Republic and the crimes the US and Israel have committed in the region,” he says.

Pezeshkian claims Washington had already seen the consequences of its actions in its own elections and among the American public. US President Donald Trump is not attending the summit, with Washington sending no official delegation for the second consecutive year.

headline: READ: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Hegseth
description: Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an effort on Tuesday to impeach Defence Secretary Pete...
article_text:
Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an effort on Tuesday to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, winning a reprieve for the polarising Pentagon chief before Democrats take control of Congress next year and possibly try again.

The vote on a procedural motion came just hours after Hegseth blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce and delivered a defiant defence of his record at the helm of the US military, winning praise from US President Donald Trump.

The chamber voted 211 to 204 in favour of a motion to refer eight articles of impeachment to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee, a move that the sponsor of the impeachment push, US Representative Thomas Massie, warned would kill it.

Massie, an outgoing Kentucky Republican, had hoped to draw votes from Republicans upset with Hegseth’s policies and wary of the unpopularity of the war on Iran, but no other Republicans joined him.

headline: ‘We’re here to do a job’: AOC criticises Democrats for missing Hegseth impeachment vote
description: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez says lawmakers need to show up and do their jobs, after 11 Democrats missed...
article_text:
Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez says lawmakers need to show up and do their jobs, after 11 Democrats missed a House vote that effectively killed an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, Al Jazeera reports.

“The people send us here to do a job,” the New York Democrat tells CNN. “I don’t know if anyone had any real health issues or anything significant. So I want to leave room for that. But that being said, at the end of the day, we’re here to do a job. And the same way I had to clock in when I worked at a restaurant, we got to clock in and do our work here.”

She says she hoped Congress would not have to wait for the new session to move against Hegseth.

headline: CDA challenges court order protecting Bari Imam House from demolition in Islamabad
description: Says property is an unauthorised encroachment on land acquired in 1963 and that no building by that name exists in its official revenue or acquisition record.
author: Malik Asad
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has pointed to serious violations at Bari Imam House in Nurpur Shahan, saying the property is an unauthorised encroachment on land acquired in 1963 and that no building by that name exists in its official revenue or acquisition record.

The authority has filed an application in the Islamabad High Court seeking an early hearing of the writ petition filed by the premises’ caretaker, Mohammad Akmal, and has decided to challenge the interim order that currently shields the structure from demolition, according to a Dawn report.

The CDA sealed Bari Imam House on Oct 30 in a joint operation with the district administration, claiming the structure stands on government land and was among properties identified in its anti-encroachment drive.

On Nov 3, the IHC issued notice to the respondents and directed them to file reports and para-wise comments within two weeks.

It also granted a mandatory injunction directing officials to “forthwith de-seal” the premises and restraining them from carrying out any “demolition” until the next hearing. The petition is presently fixed for Jan 18, 2027.

In its application, the CDA says the mandatory directions were passed on the first date of hearing without obtaining or considering its report and comments. It has raised serious objections to the maintainability of the petition, particularly regarding the petitioner’s locus standi and alleged entitlement to invoke constitutional jurisdiction.

The authority says the entire area of Mauza Nurpur Shahan was acquired under Award No. 4/DC CDA/1963 and that compensation and admissible benefits were paid to landowners. The land comprising Khasra Nos. 435, 582, 591, 592 and 593 formed part of that acquisition, and the 1963 record contains no mention of any Bari Imam House on it.

The CDA further states that the shrine land is recorded on entirely different Khasra numbers – 277, 665, 677, 678, 679 and 680 – in the name of Darbar Aalia Hazrat Bari Abdul Latif Shah. That land, it says, is across the road and distinct from the acquired land both in location and revenue record.

The premises described by the petitioner neither form part of the shrine nor fall within the Darbar’s land, the authority maintains, adding that the subject land vests in the CDA and the petitioner has no lawful right, title or interest in it. His occupation, the application says, is wholly unauthorised and amounts to encroachment.

The caretaker’s petition claims the house, located opposite the shrine of Hazrat Bari Imam Sarkar, comprises a mosque and a Langarkhana. It says the land was exempted shrine property that was never acquired, no award was announced, and no compensation was paid. It alleges the premises were sealed without notice or hearing and that an Auqaf Department board was installed at the gate, in violation of constitutional provisions.

headline: Man murdered ‘at the behest of wife, son’ in Gujrat
description: Police and Punjab Forensic Science Agency teams have collected evidence from the crime scene.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
GUJRAT: A man was allegedly shot dead by four unidentified suspects, in alleged connivance with his son and wife, at Kulachor village in Jalalpur Jattan Saddar police precincts.

Complainant Aftab Warraich, alleged in his complaint lodged with the police that his brother Fiaz, who had returned from Iran last week, was gunned down by four unidentified suspects.

He alleged that his brother’s son Ali Hasan and wife Kausar Bibi had a domestic dispute with the victim and they plotted the murder.

He also alleged that the mother and the son were present at the scene when the victim was killed, and they fled away, along with the killers, on motorcycles.

On being called, police and Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) teams reached the spot and collected evidence from the crime scene.

The body was shifted to the Aziz Bhatti Shaheed Teaching Hospital (ABSTH), where doctors conducted autopsy and handed it over to the victim’s relatives.

Police claimed to have arrested Hasan and Kausar and registered a case against the four unidentified attackers and the two nominated suspects, under sections 302, 109, 148 and 149 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

YOUTH RAPED: A village barber allegedly raped a male student of the University of Gujrat (UoG) at Chak Bhula in Gujrat Saddar police precincts.

As per the police, a UoG student, ‘W’, alleged in his complaint that his friend ‘Y’, who runs a barber shop at the village, called him to the shop where he raped him at gunpoint.

He also alleged that he filmed the episode with his phone camera and started blackmailing him. He said that the suspect had so far extorted at least Rs0.5 million from him through blackmail.

The police have registered a case against the suspect under Section 376 of the Pakistan Penal Code and started investigation.

headline: Eight indicted in foreign women’s rape case
description: Judge directs prosecution to present its witnesses on Dec 9 so the formal trial proceedings could be commenced.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: A sessions court on Tuesday indicted eight suspects, including one reportedly linked to a senior minister, in a case of alleged gang rape of two foreign women.

All the suspects, presently in judicial custody, were produced before the trial court for the indictment proceedings.

Additional District & Sessions Judge (AD&SJ) Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed the charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty.

The judge directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on Dec 9 so the formal trial proceedings could be commenced.

Separately, the judge gave the last opportunity to the prosecution to present its arguments on the post-arrest bail petitions of three of the suspects in the case.

The judge observed that the prosecution had availed multiple opportunities to argue the bail petitions on one pretext or the other.

The judge adjourned the bail hearing till Nov 11 (today) with a clear warning to the prosecution to present its arguments, otherwise, the petitions would be decided in light of the case record.

Advocate Salman Shahid had already concluded his arguments on behalf of the petitioners/suspects.

Defence-C police in its challan (investigation report) had cleared five suspects, including the one linked to the senior political figure, of sexual assault charges and implicated them in minor offences of illegal detention and extortion.

The police charged three other suspects, who were allegedly low-paid employees of one of the key suspects, with sexually assaulting the women.

All the suspects, presently in judicial custody, were produced before the trial court for the indictment proceedings.

Additional District & Sessions Judge (AD&SJ) Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed the charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty.

The judge directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on Dec 9 so the formal trial proceedings could be commenced.

Separately, the judge gave the last opportunity to the prosecution to present its arguments on the post-arrest bail petitions of three of the suspects in the case.

The judge observed that the prosecution had availed multiple opportunities to argue the bail petitions on one pretext or the other.

The judge adjourned the bail hearing till Nov 11 (today) with a clear warning to the prosecution to present its arguments, otherwise, the petitions would be decided in light of the case record.

Advocate Salman Shahid had already concluded his arguments on behalf of the petitioners/suspects.

Defence-C police in its challan (investigation report) had cleared five suspects, including the one linked to the senior political figure, of sexual assault charges and implicated them in minor offences of illegal detention and extortion.

The police charged three other suspects, who were allegedly low-paid employees of one of the key suspects, with sexually assaulting the women.

headline: Hammad Azhar complains of ‘CCTV surveillance in prison cell’
description: ATC Judge Manzer Ali Gill adjourns hearing till Nov 24 and sends Azhar back to judicial custody till the next hearing.
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: PTI leader Hammad Azhar on Tuesday complained to an antiterrorism court (ATC) about inadequate facilities in jail, alleging he had been kept under constant surveillance through two CCTV cameras installed in his cell, including one monitoring even the bathroom.

Earlier, he was produced before the court after his 14-day judicial remand in the Jinnah House attack case related to the May 9 riots expired.

His counsel, Abuzar Salman Niazi, also filed an application seeking B-class facilities for his client and removal of cameras from his cell, arguing that the gadgets violated the prisoner’s right to privacy.

Addressing the court, Azhar said he had to bathe with his clothes on because of the CCTV cameras monitoring him.

He also complained that there was neither a bed nor a mattress in his cell and he had to sleep on the floor. However, he added that he had now become accustomed to sleeping on the floor.

Azhar claimed he was being kept in the same cell where the former prime minister and PPP founder Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was detained several decades ago before his hanging. He added he was writing a book about his jail experiences and wanted future generations to read it.

The PTI leader requested the court to provide him with at least a chair and a table in his cell, so that he could continue writing. “I can manage without a bed or mattress,” he added.

Meanwhile, the investigating officer informed the court that a supplementary investigation report against Azhar was being prepared, seeking more time from the court. ATC Judge Manzer Ali Gill adjourned the hearing till Nov 24 and sent Azhar back to judicial custody till the next hearing.

Sarwar Road police had booked several PTI leaders and workers, including Azhar, on charges of attacking and vandalising the Jinnah House during the May 9 protests against the arrest of former prime minister Imran Khan.

Azhar was arrested in September this year after over three years of hiding.

CASE DISCHARGED: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday discharged an abduction and robbery case registered against two suspects allegedly involved in the Azeri woman’s gang-rape case.

Earlier, the Ichhra police produced the key suspect and a co-suspect before the magistrate.

The complainant, Shoaib Butt, told the court that the suspects had been wrongly identified “due to a misunderstanding” and that they were not the culprits. He also stated that he had no objection if the court discharged the case against them.

The magistrate discharged the case against both suspects in the light of the complainant’s statement.

The key suspect had been arrested by police in an abduction and robbery case after securing bail in the alleged gang-rape case involving a foreigner, registered by the Defence C police.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: JUI-F to protest anti-encroachment drive, ‘propaganda’ against Fazl on 15th
description: Asks govt to focus on its ‘mandate of eliminating terrorism’
author: Bureau Report
article_text:
PESHAWAR: The Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Tuesday directed its district chapters to hold street protests on Nov 15 against the ongoing drive against encroachments and “propaganda” against the party and its leadership.

Addressing a presser at the party’s provincial headquarters here after a meeting of the JUI-F KP executive council, the party’s provincial emir, Senator Maulana Attaur Rahman, said the meeting discussed “baseless and fake propaganda” against the party and its leaders, actions being taken in the name of removing encroachments and party chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman’s stand on mineral reserves.

He said it appeared that the emergency had been imposed in the province not to eliminate terrorism but to remove encroachments.

Asks govt to focus on its ‘mandate of eliminating terrorism’

Mr Atta asked the current provincial government to focus on its mandate of eliminating terrorism instead of targeting public properties across the province in the name of removing encroachments.

He said that if encroachment removal was the government’s only objective, there had been no need to impose governor’s rule and emergency in the province.

The JUI-F KP emir said the crackdown on encroachments amounted to an operation against the province’s peaceful people, who were earning livelihoods through businesses.

He said the party’s executive council had also expressed concern over the actions taken in the name of removing encroachments across the province, especially in Peshawar, including the demolition of legal shops, plazas, houses and mosques.

The council also expressed complete solidarity with the trader community and affected shopkeepers.

Mr Atta said the forum insisted that constructions on government land fell under the category of encroachments.

He said people had the right to know the justification for demolishing plazas and houses without serving notices despite the owners having obtained no-objection certificates and approval of building plans from government institutions.

The emir said that the government should assure people that compensation would be paid for properties it acquired under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act.

He also said the party had expressed concern over “irresponsible” statements by the KP governor and the adviser on information regarding the party’s Mufti Mahmood Markaz.

Mr Atta said that the complex, spread over four kanals, had been constructed after the building plans were approved by the Peshawar Development Authority.

He added that the administration had closed the service road in front of the building due to security reasons.

The JUI-F leader said the executive council fully endorsed Maulana Fazl’s stand on mineral resources.

He added that the province’s mineral resources were being transported through the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor route after the closure of roads.

“The nation should be informed about the agreements made with any country and that the party’s KP chapter stands fully with the party chief on this stance,” he said.

Mr Atta said that the council had also decided to launch an awareness campaign on the issue. He said protest demonstrations would be held in all districts of the province on Sunday (Nov 15).

He said the party’s general council had condemned “one-sided propaganda, fake statements and immoral videos” released against the JUI-F chief and other leaders. “Instead of providing reasoned and factual answers to Maulana Fazl’s questions, the federal government had resorted to cheap tactics.

The government’s paid TikTokers can’t divert the JUI-F from its mission through unethical acts and cheap tactics,” he said.

Regarding the merged tribal districts, Mr Atta said the government was trying to reverse the Fata-KP merger.

He, however, said the party believed that both the merger and any decision to reverse it should be made in accordance with the wishes of the people instead of being imposed on them.

Mr Atta said the meeting also expressed concern over the arrest of JUI-F workers in different parts of the country and notices issued by various institutions.

Addressing a presser at the party’s provincial headquarters here after a meeting of the JUI-F KP executive council, the party’s provincial emir, Senator Maulana Attaur Rahman, said the meeting discussed “baseless and fake propaganda” against the party and its leaders, actions being taken in the name of removing encroachments and party chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman’s stand on mineral reserves.

He said it appeared that the emergency had been imposed in the province not to eliminate terrorism but to remove encroachments.

Asks govt to focus on its ‘mandate of eliminating terrorism’

Mr Atta asked the current provincial government to focus on its mandate of eliminating terrorism instead of targeting public properties across the province in the name of removing encroachments.

He said that if encroachment removal was the government’s only objective, there had been no need to impose governor’s rule and emergency in the province.

The JUI-F KP emir said the crackdown on encroachments amounted to an operation against the province’s peaceful people, who were earning livelihoods through businesses.

He said the party’s executive council had also expressed concern over the actions taken in the name of removing encroachments across the province, especially in Peshawar, including the demolition of legal shops, plazas, houses and mosques.

The council also expressed complete solidarity with the trader community and affected shopkeepers.

Mr Atta said the forum insisted that constructions on government land fell under the category of encroachments.

He said people had the right to know the justification for demolishing plazas and houses without serving notices despite the owners having obtained no-objection certificates and approval of building plans from government institutions.

The emir said that the government should assure people that compensation would be paid for properties it acquired under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act.

He also said the party had expressed concern over “irresponsible” statements by the KP governor and the adviser on information regarding the party’s Mufti Mahmood Markaz.

Mr Atta said that the complex, spread over four kanals, had been constructed after the building plans were approved by the Peshawar Development Authority.

He added that the administration had closed the service road in front of the building due to security reasons.

The JUI-F leader said the executive council fully endorsed Maulana Fazl’s stand on mineral resources.

He added that the province’s mineral resources were being transported through the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor route after the closure of roads.

“The nation should be informed about the agreements made with any country and that the party’s KP chapter stands fully with the party chief on this stance,” he said.

Mr Atta said that the council had also decided to launch an awareness campaign on the issue. He said protest demonstrations would be held in all districts of the province on Sunday (Nov 15).

He said the party’s general council had condemned “one-sided propaganda, fake statements and immoral videos” released against the JUI-F chief and other leaders. “Instead of providing reasoned and factual answers to Maulana Fazl’s questions, the federal government had resorted to cheap tactics.

The government’s paid TikTokers can’t divert the JUI-F from its mission through unethical acts and cheap tactics,” he said.

Regarding the merged tribal districts, Mr Atta said the government was trying to reverse the Fata-KP merger.

He, however, said the party believed that both the merger and any decision to reverse it should be made in accordance with the wishes of the people instead of being imposed on them.

Mr Atta said the meeting also expressed concern over the arrest of JUI-F workers in different parts of the country and notices issued by various institutions.

headline: Two killed in firing over TikTok video dispute in Charsadda
description: One of the deceased was a passerby, who is said to have been caught in crossfire.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
CHARSADDA: Two people, including a passer-by, were killed in an exchange of fire between two rival groups over a dispute involving a TikTok video in the Majoki area within the jurisdiction of Parang police station on Tuesday.

Police said Adnan, son of Tariq and a resident of Parang Majoki, and passer-by Asghar Ali were killed in the firing.

In her statement to the police, Adnan’s mother, Zakia Begum, said she was present with her sons, Waqar and Adnan, when the nominated suspects, including Hilal, Babu and Asif’s wife, allegedly arrived at the scene and opened fire on them. As a result, Adnan sustained fatal bullet injuries. She cited a previous dispute over a TikTok video as the motive behind the incident.

Meanwhile, Saleem Jan, brother of the deceased passer-by Asghar Ali, told police that his brother was caught in the crossfire between two rival groups, identified as Waqar and others on one side and Hilal and others on the other, and was killed.

Police have registered cases on the reports of both the parties and launched an investigation. The TikTok video dispute is stated to be the cause of the firing.

headline: Jirga in Mirpur Bhutto ends 14-year-old hostility involving five communities
description: Another Jirga in Shikarpur settles six-year-old dispute between two communities.
author: Dawn Report
article_text:
LARKANA / SUKKUR: A Jirga (tribal court) settled multiple disputes involving five different communities to bring an end to bloodshed in tit-for-tat attacks continuing for about 14 years in the riverine area of Naudero.

The Jirga, held in Mirpur Bhutto on Monday evening, was jointly presided over by Amir Bakhsh Bhutto, Abid Jatoi, Pir Junaid Shah Rashidi, Muazzam Abbasi, Hussain Bakhsh Narejo, Pir Dinal Shah, Azhar Khan Kamario and heads of certain other communities involved in the disputes.

The meeting imposed heavy fines on the communities found responsible for murders, injuries and property damage caused to their rivals. The total amount of fines came to Rs15.8 million.

During the proceedings, representatives of the Bhutto, Kuriya and Narejo communities appeared on behalf of one party and those of the Khokhar and Kharoos communities for the other.

Their arguments were weighed by consultants, who assisted the heads of the pleading communities to reach case-to-case decisions.

After prolonged consultations, the Jirga pronounced its ruling, according to which a fine of Rs9.5 million was imposed on the side comprising the Bhutto, Kuriya and Narejo communities. The Khokhar-Kharoos side was ordered to pay a fine of Rs6.3 million to its rivals.

Another Jirga in Shikarpur settles six-year-old dispute between two communities

The ruling was accepted by the two sides and they declared an end to their long-running hostilities.

The community elders and members of the embattled rivals embraced each other after the Jirga proceedings. The Jirga warned that an additional fine of Rs4 million would be imposed if any side violated the ruling.

The settlement sent a wave of joy across the Naudero riverine area with thousands of people greeting each other over the expected end to bloodshed and tension after 14 years of feud violence. They were telling their rivals that the settlement would not only restore law and order in this riverine area, but would also improve inter-community relationship.

Extraordinary security arrangements were made for the holding of the Jirga.

The community heads noted that the Khokhar-Kharoos side disowned two murders, of Imamuddin Narejo and Azeem Kuriya, and causing injuries to another man, Sarwar Kuriya. The Jirga kept the matter pending and bound down the two sides to ensure provision of related evidence.

Chandio-Magsi feud

Another Jirga, held in Qambar town, settled an old dispute between the Chandio and Magsi communities by imposing heavy fines on both the sides and ordering them to stop further bloodshed.

A fine of Rs8.3 million was imposed on the Magsi side over killing a young man, Suleman Chandio, and wounding two others two years ago in Qambar’s Ghausia locality.

The Jirga was chaired by PPP MPA Burhan Khan Chandio, who found accused Ali Jan Magsi guilty of the murder.

Both sides accepted the ruling and part of the fine amount, Rs500,000, was deposited with the Jirga on behalf of the Magsi side. The remaining amount was pledged to be paid off in two installments.

Shikarpur Jirga

In Shikarpur, a Jirga settled a six-year-old dispute between the Jeeha and Dahani communities. The hostility had claimed no fewer than 26 lives.

The Jirga was presided over by Sardar Zulfiqar Khan Kamario and MPA Mir Nadir Khan Magsi at Kamariyo House in Tarai village of Shikarpur district.

On behalf of the Jeeha community, Sardarzada Azhar Khan Kamario, MPA Mohammad Arif Khan Mahar, Sardar Zulfiqar Khan Sarki, Sardarzada Najaf Khan Kamario, Dr Saleem Khan Abro, Wadero Ghulam Mustafa Kakhirani, and others acted as advisers.

On behalf of the Dahani community, Sardar Moazzam Khan Abbasi, Sardar Attaullah Khan Buledi, Sardar Agha Ali Nawaz Khan Jalbani, Rehan Khan Buledi, Ali Hassan Dahani and served as advisers.

Both sides presented their respective accounts of the incidents leading to each and every casualty and loss of properties. Most of the violent incidents appeared to be related to ‘honour’.

After several hours of consultations between community elders and their advisers in a closed session, the Jirga ruling was pronounced.

The Dahani community was ordered to pay Rs46.7million to the rival side on account of 13 murders and the death of a woman who was caught in crossfire.

The Jeeha community was ordered to pay a fine of Rs40.2 million to the other side against murder of nine people, including two women and a minor girl.

A large number of people belonging to the rival communities celebrated the peaceful settlement of the dispute.

The area police escorted the community elders and their advisers back to their homes under stringent security arrangements made across the routes.

The hostility between the two sides had begun over a couple’s freewill marriage.

article_html:
LARKANA / SUKKUR: A Jirga (tribal court) settled multiple disputes involving five different communities to bring an end to bloodshed in tit-for-tat attacks continuing for about 14 years in the riverine area of Naudero.

The Jirga, held in Mirpur Bhutto on Monday evening, was jointly presided over by Amir Bakhsh Bhutto, Abid Jatoi, Pir Junaid Shah Rashidi, Muazzam Abbasi, Hussain Bakhsh Narejo, Pir Dinal Shah, Azhar Khan Kamario and heads of certain other communities involved in the disputes.

The meeting imposed heavy fines on the communities found responsible for murders, injuries and property damage caused to their rivals. The total amount of fines came to Rs15.8 million.

During the proceedings, representatives of the Bhutto, Kuriya and Narejo communities appeared on behalf of one party and those of the Khokhar and Kharoos communities for the other.

Their arguments were weighed by consultants, who assisted the heads of the pleading communities to reach case-to-case decisions.

After prolonged consultations, the Jirga pronounced its ruling, according to which a fine of Rs9.5 million was imposed on the side comprising the Bhutto, Kuriya and Narejo communities. The Khokhar-Kharoos side was ordered to pay a fine of Rs6.3 million to its rivals.

Another Jirga in Shikarpur settles six-year-old dispute between two communities

The ruling was accepted by the two sides and they declared an end to their long-running hostilities.

The community elders and members of the embattled rivals embraced each other after the Jirga proceedings. The Jirga warned that an additional fine of Rs4 million would be imposed if any side violated the ruling.

The settlement sent a wave of joy across the Naudero riverine area with thousands of people greeting each other over the expected end to bloodshed and tension after 14 years of feud violence. They were telling their rivals that the settlement would not only restore law and order in this riverine area, but would also improve inter-community relationship.

Extraordinary security arrangements were made for the holding of the Jirga.

The community heads noted that the Khokhar-Kharoos side disowned two murders, of Imamuddin Narejo and Azeem Kuriya, and causing injuries to another man, Sarwar Kuriya. The Jirga kept the matter pending and bound down the two sides to ensure provision of related evidence.

Chandio-Magsi feud

Another Jirga, held in Qambar town, settled an old dispute between the Chandio and Magsi communities by imposing heavy fines on both the sides and ordering them to stop further bloodshed.

A fine of Rs8.3 million was imposed on the Magsi side over killing a young man, Suleman Chandio, and wounding two others two years ago in Qambar’s Ghausia locality.

The Jirga was chaired by PPP MPA Burhan Khan Chandio, who found accused Ali Jan Magsi guilty of the murder.

Both sides accepted the ruling and part of the fine amount, Rs500,000, was deposited with the Jirga on behalf of the Magsi side. The remaining amount was pledged to be paid off in two installments.

Shikarpur Jirga

In Shikarpur, a Jirga settled a six-year-old dispute between the Jeeha and Dahani communities. The hostility had claimed no fewer than 26 lives.

The Jirga was presided over by Sardar Zulfiqar Khan Kamario and MPA Mir Nadir Khan Magsi at Kamariyo House in Tarai village of Shikarpur district.

On behalf of the Jeeha community, Sardarzada Azhar Khan Kamario, MPA Mohammad Arif Khan Mahar, Sardar Zulfiqar Khan Sarki, Sardarzada Najaf Khan Kamario, Dr Saleem Khan Abro, Wadero Ghulam Mustafa Kakhirani, and others acted as advisers.

On behalf of the Dahani community, Sardar Moazzam Khan Abbasi, Sardar Attaullah Khan Buledi, Sardar Agha Ali Nawaz Khan Jalbani, Rehan Khan Buledi, Ali Hassan Dahani and served as advisers.

Both sides presented their respective accounts of the incidents leading to each and every casualty and loss of properties. Most of the violent incidents appeared to be related to ‘honour’.

After several hours of consultations between community elders and their advisers in a closed session, the Jirga ruling was pronounced.

The Dahani community was ordered to pay Rs46.7million to the rival side on account of 13 murders and the death of a woman who was caught in crossfire.

The Jeeha community was ordered to pay a fine of Rs40.2 million to the other side against murder of nine people, including two women and a minor girl.

A large number of people belonging to the rival communities celebrated the peaceful settlement of the dispute.

The area police escorted the community elders and their advisers back to their homes under stringent security arrangements made across the routes.

The hostility between the two sides had begun over a couple’s freewill marriage.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: US Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats: reports
description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently moved from his Washington, DC residence to a US military base after...
article_text:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently moved from his Washington, DC residence to a US military base after Iranian threats against his life, reports Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter.

The New York Times first reported the move.

“The secretary will not be deterred by the Iranian regime’s threats and remains committed to executing Operation Economic Outcast and maintaining the blockade, which together are collapsing Iran’s economy,” a US Treasury spokesperson said in an emailed statement to Reuters.

The Times reported the severity of the threats to Bessent was not immediately clear.

headline: Fire destroys hotel’s hall during Diwali celebration in Sukkur
description: Hotel management has confirmed that the blaze was caused by the fireworks set off during the celebration.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
SUKKUR: A wedding hall was destroyed when firecrackers caused a big fire inside during a function held to celebrate Diwali on Monday night.

Each and everything, including fixture and furniture, electrical and electronic apparatuses, equipment and carpets and curtains, were reduced to ashes, owners of the Pakistan Club Hotel that houses the hall, said, adding that the losses ran into millions of rupees.

Management of the hotel, located near the City Point Bypass, confirmed to local reporters that the blaze was caused by the fireworks set off during the celebration.

According to the hotel staff, people started rushing to safety as soon as the fire intensified. They said no one was killed or injured in the incident.

Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

headline: Transit strike over high fuel prices blocks roads in Chile
description: Hundreds of truckers and bus drivers in Chile launched an indefinite strike on Tuesday to protest high fuel prices,...
article_text:
Hundreds of truckers and bus drivers in Chile launched an indefinite strike on Tuesday to protest high fuel prices, blocking roads and major highways, AFP reports.

Hndreds of transport workers gathered at various points of Route 5, which runs the length of Chile from north to south, to demand relief from surging diesel prices, which are widely relied on in the sector.

The average price of diesel has risen 74 percent since March — driven by the war in Iran — threatening many transport companies, according to industry groups.

A Tuesday afternoon meeting between government officials and protest leaders failed to reach a resolution.

headline: Fight or flight? Trump mixes signals after midterms
description: He has admitted that the Iran war was largely to blame for the midterms rout; But has strongly backed Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth’s battle against impeachment.
author: AFP
article_text:
President Donald Trump’s political mantra is “fight, fight, fight.” But he has given decidedly mixed messages about whether he will do so after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.

In the week since becoming a lame duck, Trump named the hardline architect of his migration crackdown as his chief of staff, while admitting his deportation policy was too tough.

The 80-year-old raised eyebrows when he publicly asked Ultimate Fighting Championship boss Dana White to be his new press secretary — then claimed he was just joking.

He has admitted that the Iran war was largely to blame for the midterms rout. But he has strongly backed Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth’s battle against impeachment.

And despite saying on election night that he’d accept the results of the Democratic sweep, he has reverted to type and revived baseless claims of election fraud.

“One of the characteristics of Donald Trump is that he changes his mind on a dime,” Democratic Senator Chris Coons told CNN.

“He’ll be praising someone on Monday, firing them on Tuesday, and pretending he never knew them on Wednesday. So it’s hard to predict exactly what Donald Trump is going to do.”

‘Too tough’

Democrats have promised to rein in Trump and launch a series of investigations into corruption and abuse of power. He could face a third impeachment.

But for a president supposedly facing his last stand, he has at times struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone. As results came in, he congratulated Democrats on seizing Congress and said he could work with them.

Instead of a press conference the next day, he gave reporters a tour of his new White House ballroom — sparking speculation he might spend the rest of his term on his building projects.

But the signs of volatility were still there. In the Oval Office, Trump placed a red baseball cap saying “veto” on his desk.

And when Trump announced on Friday that ultraloyalist Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as his chief of staff, it seemed that the gloves were finally off.

The brains behind the masked immigration raids that left two Americans dead, Miller has also been instrumental in using executive orders to help Trump bypass Congress.

Yet in an interview the same day — though broadcast on Sunday — Trump conceded voters had been turned off by the aggressive deportation push.

In the week since becoming a lame duck, Trump named the hardline architect of his migration crackdown as his chief of staff, while admitting his deportation policy was too tough.

The 80-year-old raised eyebrows when he publicly asked Ultimate Fighting Championship boss Dana White to be his new press secretary — then claimed he was just joking.

He has admitted that the Iran war was largely to blame for the midterms rout. But he has strongly backed Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth’s battle against impeachment.

And despite saying on election night that he’d accept the results of the Democratic sweep, he has reverted to type and revived baseless claims of election fraud.

“One of the characteristics of Donald Trump is that he changes his mind on a dime,” Democratic Senator Chris Coons told CNN.

“He’ll be praising someone on Monday, firing them on Tuesday, and pretending he never knew them on Wednesday. So it’s hard to predict exactly what Donald Trump is going to do.”

‘Too tough’

Democrats have promised to rein in Trump and launch a series of investigations into corruption and abuse of power. He could face a third impeachment.

But for a president supposedly facing his last stand, he has at times struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone. As results came in, he congratulated Democrats on seizing Congress and said he could work with them.

Instead of a press conference the next day, he gave reporters a tour of his new White House ballroom — sparking speculation he might spend the rest of his term on his building projects.
